items: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU

items.function_short: Lets the gut absorb calcium and phosphate so that bone can mineralise properly.
items.function_full: Cholecalciferol is hydroxylated in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the circulating storage form measured on a blood test, and then in the kidney to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol), a steroid hormone acting through the nuclear vitamin D receptor. Calcitriol drives active intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate, suppresses parathyroid hormone, and maintains the calcium-phosphate product that osteoblasts need to mineralise newly laid osteoid. Vitamin D receptors are present in immune cells, muscle and many other tissues, but the only role with an established human requirement is the calcium and bone axis. Skin synthesis from UVB normally supplies most of it, which is why dietary requirement figures depend heavily on latitude, season and sun exposure.
items.deficiency_name: Rickets in growing children, osteomalacia in adults. Severe infant deficiency also causes hypocalcaemic seizures and dilated cardiomyopathy.
items.deficiency_early: Serum 25(OH)D falls first, then parathyroid hormone rises (secondary hyperparathyroidism) while serum calcium is still normal or low-normal. At this stage a person notices little or nothing: vague aching in the hips, ribs and shins, and proximal muscle weakness showing up as difficulty rising from a low chair or climbing stairs. A blood test shows low 25(OH)D, raised PTH and often raised alkaline phosphatase before any X-ray change.
items.deficiency_severe: In children, growth plates fail to mineralise: bowed legs or knock knees, widened wrists and ankles, the rachitic rosary at the costochondral junctions, delayed walking, poor growth and fractures. Infants can present first with hypocalcaemic tetany, seizures or dilated cardiomyopathy, which can be fatal. In adults, unmineralised osteoid accumulates as osteomalacia, giving bone pain, proximal myopathy with a waddling gait, and Looser zones (pseudofractures) that progress to complete fractures of the pubic rami, femoral neck or ribs.
items.reversibility_note: Biochemistry, bone pain, myopathy, hypocalcaemic seizures and the radiological signs of active rickets correct completely with vitamin D plus adequate calcium, usually over weeks to a few months. Skeletal deformity already established in long-standing rickets often persists, and marked bowing, rachitic dwarfism or pelvic deformity may need surgical correction.
items.at_risk: People with little effective sun exposure: housebound or institutionalised older adults, those who cover the skin fully, and anyone living at high latitude through winter. Darker skin at high latitude (more melanin means less UVB synthesis). Exclusively breastfed infants not given a supplement, since breast milk is low in vitamin D. Obesity (sequestration in adipose tissue). Fat malabsorption from coeliac disease, cystic fibrosis, cholestasis or bariatric surgery. Chronic kidney or liver disease, and long-term anticonvulsant or glucocorticoid therapy.
items.prevalence: NHANES 2011-2014: 5.0% of the US population aged 1 year and over had serum 25(OH)D below 30 nmol/L (at risk of deficiency) and 18.3% fell between 30 and 49.9 nmol/L; the below-30 figure was 17.5% in non-Hispanic Black participants against 2.1% in non-Hispanic White participants (PMID 31076739). Clinical nutritional rickets is uncommon in high-income countries but has not disappeared, and remains common in parts of the Middle East, Africa and South Asia (PMID 26741135).
items.source: PMID 31076739 (Herrick KA et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2019, Vitamin D status in the United States 2011-2014); PMID 26741135 (Munns CF et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016, Global Consensus Recommendations on Prevention and Management of Nutritional Rickets)

items.supplement: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
items.function_short: The body's main fat-soluble antioxidant, protecting cell membranes and nerves from oxidative damage.
items.function_full: Alpha-tocopherol is the only form of vitamin E the body retains. After absorption, hepatic alpha-tocopherol transfer protein (TTPA) selectively loads alpha-tocopherol onto VLDL for export to tissues, while the other tocopherols and the tocotrienols are metabolised and excreted. Its established function is to break the chain reaction of lipid peroxidation in the polyunsaturated fatty acids of cell membranes and lipoproteins, donating a hydrogen atom to lipid peroxyl radicals and then being regenerated by ascorbate. The tissues that suffer first without it are peripheral nerve axons, the posterior columns and cerebellum, the retina, and the erythrocyte membrane. A 400 IU dose is roughly 20 to 27 times the adult RDA of 15 mg/d, so at that level it is being used pharmacologically rather than to correct any dietary shortfall.
items.deficiency_name: No classic single-name disease. The recognised syndrome is vitamin E deficiency ataxia, a spinocerebellar degeneration with peripheral neuropathy and pigmentary retinopathy; in preterm infants it presents as haemolytic anaemia of prematurity. Ataxia with isolated vitamin E deficiency (AVED) produces the same clinical picture but is an inherited TTPA gene defect, not a dietary deficiency.
items.deficiency_early: Plasma alpha-tocopherol below roughly 12 micromol/L, or a low tocopherol-to-total-lipid ratio, precedes symptoms by months to years and is the practical marker. The first clinical signs are loss of ankle reflexes and reduced vibration and joint position sense in the feet, sometimes with unsteady walking in the dark. In preterm infants, a haemolytic anaemia with raised reticulocytes.
items.deficiency_severe: Untreated, it progresses to a combined spinocerebellar and sensory picture: ataxia from posterior column degeneration, dysarthria, ophthalmoplegia, head titubation, proximal weakness, and pigmentary retinopathy with declining visual acuity. The endpoint is a person who can no longer walk unaided, with fixed sensory ataxia and neuropathy.
items.reversibility_note: High-dose repletion reliably halts progression, and when started early (within roughly a year of symptom onset, or before symptoms in a child with known malabsorption) much of the neuropathy recovers. Long-standing posterior column and cerebellar degeneration and established retinopathy usually do not fully resolve, so treatment prevents more than it restores.
items.at_risk: Almost exclusively people who cannot absorb fat: cystic fibrosis, cholestatic liver disease and biliary atresia, short bowel syndrome, chronic pancreatitis, abetalipoproteinaemia and homozygous hypobetalipoproteinaemia. Preterm and very low birth weight infants. Separately, people with the inherited TTPA defect (AVED), which is a genetic transport disorder rather than a consequence of diet. In an adult with normal fat absorption, eating too little vitamin E essentially does not produce clinical deficiency.
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED for frank clinical deficiency, which is rare enough in the general population that no meaningful prevalence figure exists. The widely quoted claim that over 90% of Americans fail to meet the estimated average requirement for alpha-tocopherol is an intake statistic, not a deficiency rate, and no corresponding burden of neurological disease accompanies it (doi:10.3945/an.114.006254). Biochemical deficiency is common in untreated cystic fibrosis and cholestatic liver disease.
items.source: doi:10.3945/an.114.006254 (Traber MG, Adv Nutr 2014, Vitamin E inadequacy in humans: causes and consequences); PMID 15681888 (cerebellar ataxia due to isolated vitamin E deficiency); PMID 35727271 (USPSTF Recommendation Statement, JAMA 2022, D recommendation against vitamin E for CVD or cancer prevention)

items.supplement: Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU
items.function_short: Makes the eye's dim-light pigment and keeps skin, gut and airway linings healthy.
items.function_full: Retinol is oxidised to 11-cis-retinal, which binds opsin to form rhodopsin, the photopigment of the rod cells that makes vision in dim light possible. By a separate route it is oxidised to all-trans and 9-cis retinoic acid, ligands for the nuclear RAR and RXR receptors, which regulate transcription of genes controlling epithelial differentiation (goblet cells and mucin production in the conjunctiva, cornea, respiratory tract and gut), embryonic patterning, haematopoiesis, and both innate and adaptive immunity including gut-homing of T lymphocytes. Preformed retinol from liver, dairy, eggs and supplements is absorbed efficiently and stored in hepatic stellate cells, which buffer plasma concentrations for months. 10,000 IU is about 3,000 micrograms retinol activity equivalents, roughly four times the adult RDA and at the tolerable upper intake level, so at this dose the clinically relevant question is excess rather than shortfall.
items.deficiency_name: Xerophthalmia, the spectrum running from night blindness (nyctalopia) through conjunctival and corneal xerosis to keratomalacia.
items.deficiency_early: Impaired dark adaptation, then frank night blindness: trouble seeing after dusk or in a dimly lit room, which in a small child shows as reluctance to move about after dark. Conjunctival xerosis and Bitot spots, foamy grey triangular patches of keratinised conjunctiva, follow. Increased severity and duration of measles, diarrhoea and respiratory infection often precede any eye sign. Serum retinol below 0.70 micromol/L is the biochemical marker, though it falls only once liver stores are largely gone.
items.deficiency_severe: Corneal xerosis progresses to punctate keratopathy, then corneal ulceration, then keratomalacia, in which the corneal stroma liquefies over a few days and frequently perforates. The eye is structurally destroyed and blindness is permanent. Deficiency also substantially raises child mortality from measles, diarrhoeal disease and respiratory infection, and roughly half of the children who go blind from it die within twelve months.
items.reversibility_note: Night blindness, conjunctival xerosis and Bitot spots reverse within days to weeks of high-dose retinol. Once the cornea ulcerates or melts, the loss is structural and permanent, and vitamin A deficiency remains a leading cause of preventable childhood blindness worldwide. The window between the fully reversible and the irreversible stage can be only a few days in a sick, depleted child, which is why treatment is given on clinical suspicion without waiting for a retinol assay.
items.at_risk: Preschool children and pregnant and lactating women in low-income settings whose diets contain little animal-source food or provitamin A vegetables, particularly where measles and diarrhoeal disease are common. In high-income countries deficiency is rare and almost always secondary to disease: cystic fibrosis, cholestatic liver disease, short bowel syndrome, pancreatic insufficiency and bariatric surgery. It also occurs with extremely restricted eating, including the food selectivity seen in some autistic children, where xerophthalmia has been reported.
items.prevalence: WHO estimated that for 1995-2005, 190 million preschool-age children (33.3% of that age group in at-risk populations) and 19.1 million pregnant women had serum retinol below 0.70 micromol/L, with about 5.2 million preschool children affected by night blindness (WHO, Global prevalence of vitamin A deficiency in populations at risk 1995-2005, Geneva 2009). Deficiency in high-income populations is rare and disease-related rather than dietary; no useful population prevalence figure exists for those settings.
items.source: WHO, Global prevalence of vitamin A deficiency in populations at risk 1995-2005, WHO Global Database on Vitamin A Deficiency, Geneva 2009 (ISBN 978 92 4 159801 9); PMID 18806089 (Sommer A, J Nutr 2008, Vitamin A deficiency and clinical disease: an historical overview)

items.function_short: A plant pigment the body can turn into vitamin A; nothing in the body needs it directly.
items.function_full: Beta-carotene is a provitamin A carotenoid, the orange pigment of carrots, sweet potato, pumpkin and dark green leaves. In the intestinal mucosa, beta-carotene 15,15'-oxygenase (BCO1) cleaves it to retinal, which is reduced to retinol and esterified for storage. The conversion is feedback-regulated and inefficient: the Institute of Medicine assigns 12 micrograms of dietary beta-carotene the vitamin A activity of 1 microgram of retinol, and common BCO1 variants reduce conversion markedly in a substantial minority of people. Uncleaved beta-carotene acts as a lipid-phase antioxidant and singlet oxygen quencher in laboratory systems, but no human physiological process depends on the intact molecule, and every requirement it can meet is a vitamin A requirement that preformed retinol meets directly.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. Nobody becomes beta-carotene deficient. A diet containing no beta-carotene at all is nutritionally complete provided preformed vitamin A is supplied. For this compound the clinically established direction of effect is harm at supplemental doses rather than any deficiency risk: in the ATBC and CARET trials, 20 to 30 mg/d increased lung cancer incidence and total mortality in smokers and asbestos-exposed workers (PMID 8127329, PMID 8602180).
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE, since no deficiency state exists. Low plasma carotenoid concentrations are a useful marker of low vegetable intake, not a diagnosis of deficiency, and they carry no defined clinical threshold.
items.source: Institute of Medicine, Dietary Reference Intakes for Vitamin A, Vitamin K, Arsenic, Boron, Chromium, Copper, Iodine, Iron, Manganese, Molybdenum, Nickel, Silicon, Vanadium and Zinc (National Academies Press, 2001), which sets no requirement for beta-carotene; PMID 8127329 (ATBC Study Group, N Engl J Med 1994;330:1029-35); PMID 8602180 (Omenn GS et al., CARET, N Engl J Med 1996;334:1150-5); PMID 35727271 (USPSTF Recommendation Statement, JAMA 2022, D recommendation against beta-carotene)

items.function_short: Activates proteins that clot blood and that steer calcium into bone rather than artery walls.
items.function_full: Every form of vitamin K works as the cofactor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, the enzyme that converts specific glutamate residues into gamma-carboxyglutamate (Gla), giving those proteins the ability to bind calcium and function. In the liver this activates clotting factors II, VII, IX and X together with the anticoagulant proteins C, S and Z, which is the function the dietary requirement is set on. Outside the liver the same reaction activates osteocalcin in bone and matrix Gla protein in vascular smooth muscle, matrix Gla protein being a local inhibitor of arterial calcification. MK-7 differs from phylloquinone (K1) mainly in pharmacokinetics: a long isoprenoid side chain gives it a circulating half-life of days rather than hours, so it reaches extrahepatic tissue more consistently. MK-4 is the form tissues synthesise for themselves from K1 or menadione via UBIAD1, and as a supplement it clears within hours. Whether raising menaquinone intake above the amount that maintains normal carboxylation changes bone or vascular outcomes is a question about supplementation, separate from the vitamin's essential role.
items.deficiency_name: Vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB), historically called haemorrhagic disease of the newborn. No deficiency disease is attributed to menaquinones specifically: intake recommendations are set for total vitamin K and are based on phylloquinone, and no separate K2 requirement has been established.
items.deficiency_early: A rising PIVKA-II (undercarboxylated prothrombin) is the earliest coagulation marker, followed by a prolonged prothrombin time and raised INR. Clinically, easy bruising, oozing from puncture or venepuncture sites, nosebleeds, bleeding gums or heavy menstrual loss. Undercarboxylated osteocalcin rises before any of the clotting markers, but on its own it is a biochemical finding whose clinical significance is unsettled.
items.deficiency_severe: In newborns, classic VKDB appears in the first week as bleeding from the umbilical stump, gastrointestinal tract, circumcision site or puncture wounds. Late VKDB appears at 2 to 12 weeks and is the dangerous form: roughly half of cases present with intracranial haemorrhage, causing death or lasting neurological injury. In adults with severe malabsorption, cholestasis or prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics plus poor intake, deficiency produces spontaneous gastrointestinal, retroperitoneal or intracranial bleeding.
items.reversibility_note: The coagulopathy itself corrects completely and quickly: parenteral vitamin K restores clotting factor activity within hours, and prothrombin complex concentrate acts immediately. What does not reverse is the injury from a bleed that has already happened, and intracranial haemorrhage in late VKDB leaves permanent neurological deficit or death in a substantial proportion of affected infants. This is why prophylaxis at birth matters more than treatment.
items.at_risk: Newborns above all, who are born with low stores, receive little vitamin K in breast milk and have an immature gut flora. Intramuscular vitamin K at birth prevents this, and declining or omitting that injection is the main cause of late VKDB in high-income countries today. Beyond infancy: fat malabsorption, cholestasis and biliary obstruction, cystic fibrosis, extensive small bowel resection, and people on vitamin K antagonists such as warfarin, in whom the deficiency is induced on purpose. Dietary vitamin K deficiency in a healthy adult is rare, because phylloquinone is abundant in green vegetables and the liver recycles it efficiently.
items.prevalence: Without prophylaxis, late VKDB occurs at roughly 4.4 to 7.2 per 100,000 births in European and Asian surveillance series, with higher rates reported from some regions, and classic VKDB affects an estimated 0.25% to 1.7% of unprophylaxed newborns (PMID 18804903). No population prevalence figure is established for clinical vitamin K deficiency in healthy adults, where it is rare. Undercarboxylated osteocalcin and inactive matrix Gla protein are detectable in a large share of adults, but that is a biomarker observation with no defined clinical deficiency threshold.
items.source: PMID 18804903 (Shearer MJ, Blood Rev 2009, Vitamin K deficiency bleeding in early infancy); doi:10.1146/annurev-nutr-080508-141217 (Booth SL, Annu Rev Nutr 2009;29:89-110, Roles for vitamin K beyond coagulation)

items.function_short: A fish-liver oil supplying vitamin D, preformed vitamin A and omega-3 fats together.
items.function_full: Cod liver oil is a food product, oil rendered from the livers of Gadus species, carrying three active constituents in one dose: vitamin D3, preformed vitamin A as retinyl esters, and the long-chain omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA. Each has its own physiology (see the vitamin D3 and preformed vitamin A entries; EPA and DHA are incorporated into membrane phospholipids and serve as precursors to eicosanoids and specialised pro-resolving mediators, with DHA concentrated in retinal photoreceptor and neuronal membranes). It has historical standing because it was the agent that treated and then largely eliminated rickets in the polluted industrial cities of the early twentieth century, before vitamin D itself had been identified. Modern products vary widely in content depending on whether the natural vitamins were stripped during refining and re-added, so the label matters. The practical constraint on dosing is the preformed retinol: an amount large enough to deliver a meaningful EPA and DHA intake can push vitamin A toward or past the tolerable upper limit, and the vitamin A here is retinol, not beta-carotene.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. Cod liver oil is a product category, not a nutrient. The relevant deficiency states belong to its constituents and are described under the vitamin D3 and preformed vitamin A entries.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. No one becomes deficient in cod liver oil. Deficiency risk attaches to its constituent nutrients, principally vitamin D, and is set out in that entry.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE, product category rather than a nutrient.
items.source: PMID 12897318 (Rajakumar K, Pediatrics 2003;112:e132-5, Vitamin D, cod-liver oil, sunlight, and rickets: a historical perspective)

items.function_short: A mixed low-dose top-up of many nutrients at once; it has no function of its own.
items.function_full: A multivitamin/multimineral is a product category rather than a substance: a fixed combination typically supplying somewhere around the RDA for ten to thirty vitamins and minerals in a single daily dose. It has no physiology of its own, and whatever it does in the body is simply the sum of the individual nutrients, each acting through its own pathway. Formulations differ enormously in which nutrients are included, in what chemical form (iron as sulphate or bisglycinate, folate as folic acid or 5-MTHF, vitamin D as D2 or D3), and at what fraction or multiple of the RDA, so trial evidence about one product transfers poorly to another. Its coherent use is as insurance against gaps in an inadequate diet. A diagnosed deficiency is treated with the specific nutrient at a therapeutic dose, which a multivitamin does not supply.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no multivitamin deficiency state. The people for whom a multivitamin is plausibly useful are those with genuinely restricted intake: older adults eating very little total food, people on restrictive or eliminated diets, those with malabsorption, and post-bariatric surgery patients (who need specific high-dose regimens with separate B12, iron and fat-soluble vitamin monitoring rather than a generic multivitamin). In pregnancy the evidence base is for folic acid and iodine specifically, not for the multivitamin as a package.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE, product category rather than a nutrient. For prevention of cardiovascular disease or cancer in generally healthy, non-pregnant adults the USPSTF concluded in 2022 that evidence is insufficient to judge the balance of benefits and harms (I statement).
items.source: PMID 35727271 (US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement, JAMA 2022;327(23):2326-2333, Vitamin, Mineral, and Multivitamin Supplementation to Prevent Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer)

errors.supplement: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
errors.correction: The text says "A 400 IU dose is roughly 20 to 27 times the adult RDA of 15 mg/d." That is IU divided by mg (400/15 = 26.7), which treats IU and mg as the same unit. Applying the actual conversions: 400 IU of natural RRR-alpha-tocopherol = 400/1.49 = 268 mg, which is 17.9 times the 15 mg RDA; 400 IU of synthetic all-rac-alpha-tocopherol = 400/2.22 = 180 mg, which is 12.0 times. The correct statement is "roughly 12 to 18 times the adult RDA, depending on whether the product is synthetic or natural-source." The error inflates the stated multiple by about 50 percent and is in the one sentence a reader uses to judge how far above physiological the dose sits.
errors.source: IOM/FDA conversion factors: 1 mg alpha-tocopherol = 1.49 IU natural (RRR) = 2.22 IU synthetic (all-rac); RDA 15 mg/d adults. NIH ODS Vitamin E Health Professional Fact Sheet; FDA 2018 final rule on units of measure (guidance doc, fda.gov/media/129863/download)

errors.correction: The entry is titled "Beta-carotene supplements" but quotes only the dietary conversion ratio (12 micrograms beta-carotene = 1 microgram retinol). The IOM sets a separate and much more favourable ratio for the supplemental form: 2 micrograms of supplemental beta-carotene in oil = 1 microgram RAE, because purified beta-carotene in an oil matrix bypasses the food-matrix release step. As written, a reader is led to understate the retinol activity of a beta-carotene capsule roughly sixfold. Add the 2:1 supplemental figure alongside the 12:1 dietary figure.
errors.source: Institute of Medicine, Dietary Reference Intakes for Vitamin A, Vitamin K, Arsenic, Boron, Chromium, Copper, Iodine, Iron, Manganese, Molybdenum, Nickel, Silicon, Vanadium and Zinc (National Academies Press, 2001), RAE definitions

errors.correction: The text says "in the ATBC and CARET trials, 20 to 30 mg/d increased lung cancer incidence and total mortality." CARET did not test beta-carotene alone: the active arm received 30 mg beta-carotene PLUS 25,000 IU retinol as retinyl palmitate daily (lung cancer RR 1.28, 95% CI 1.04-1.57; all-cause death RR 1.17). Only ATBC isolated beta-carotene as a single agent at 20 mg/d (lung cancer incidence +18%, 95% CI 3-36%; total mortality +8%, 95% CI 1-16%). The causal attribution to beta-carotene alone rests on ATBC; CARET is supporting evidence for the combination. Reword to "ATBC (beta-carotene 20 mg/d alone) and CARET (beta-carotene 30 mg/d plus retinol)."
errors.source: PMID 8127329 (ATBC, N Engl J Med 1994;330:1029-35); PMID 8602180 (Omenn GS et al., CARET, N Engl J Med 1996;334:1150-5), both verified against the published abstracts

errors.supplement: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
errors.correction: PMID 15681888 (Jayaram S et al., Indian J Med Sci 2005;59(1):20-23) is a single case report of AVED, the autosomal recessive TTPA mutation. It is cited as the clinical evidence for an entry whose deficiency_state is CLINICAL and whose own deficiency_name text correctly excludes AVED as "an inherited TTPA gene defect, not a dietary deficiency." The citation therefore does not support the acquired/malabsorptive syndrome the entry is classifying. Replace or supplement it with a malabsorption-based source (Sokol RJ's work on vitamin E deficiency neuropathy in chronic childhood cholestasis, or a cystic fibrosis series). Worth noting the cited case "responded partially to replacement," which does independently support the PARTIAL reversibility call.
errors.source: PMID 15681888 abstract, verified: "Ataxia with isolated Vit E deficiency (AVED) is an Autosomal Recessive genetic disorder with a mutation in the alpha tocopherol transfer protein gene (TTPA)"

errors.correction: Both numbers are correct in the literature (0.25% to 1.7% for classic VKDB and 4.4 to 7.2 per 100,000 for late VKDB without prophylaxis, as given by CDC/AAP), but neither appears in the cited source in that form. Shearer 2009 states 4-7 cases per 10^5 births for Europe and separately flags substantially higher rates in Southeast Asia. Describing 4.4-7.2 per 100,000 as covering "European and Asian surveillance series" folds Asia into a Western range and understates the Asian burden. Attribute the 4.4-7.2 and 0.25-1.7% figures to CDC MMWR 2013 / AAP, and keep Shearer for the European 4-7 per 100,000 plus the higher Southeast Asian rates stated separately.
errors.source: PMID 18804903 (Shearer MJ, Blood Rev 2009) abstract, verified; PMID 24226627 (MMWR, Late Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding in Infants Whose Parents Declined Vitamin K Prophylaxis, Tennessee 2013)

errors.correction: PMID 26741135 is the Horm Res Paediatr 2016;85(2):83-106 printing of the Munns Global Consensus, not the J Clin Endocrinol Metab printing the entry names. The consensus was co-published; the JCEM version (2016;101(2):394-415) is PMID 26745253. Either change the journal to Horm Res Paediatr or change the PMID to 26745253. The NHANES citation in the same field (PMID 31076739) checks out exactly: 5.0% below 30 nmol/L, 18.3% at 30-49.9 nmol/L, 17.5% non-Hispanic Black against 2.1% non-Hispanic White.
errors.source: PubMed records for PMID 26741135 (Horm Res Paediatr) and PMID 26745253 (J Clin Endocrinol Metab), both verified

misclassified.supplement: Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU
misclassified.why: The label contradicts the entry's own reversibility_note, which describes a textbook partial picture: "Night blindness, conjunctival xerosis and Bitot spots reverse within days to weeks of high-dose retinol. Once the cornea ulcerates or melts, the loss is structural and permanent." That is exactly the pattern the dataset labels PARTIAL for vitamin D (biochemistry and myopathy correct, established bowing persists), vitamin E (neuropathy recovers if treated early, posterior column degeneration does not) and vitamin K (coagulopathy corrects in hours, intracranial haemorrhage damage does not). Vitamin A is the only fat-soluble entry with the same structure given a different label. The clinical direction of the error matters: xerophthalmia is the most treatment-responsive stage-dependent deficiency in the group, night blindness resolves within days of a single high dose, and WHO/Sommer's whole case for treating on clinical suspicion without waiting for a retinol assay rests on the early stages being fully reversible. IRREVERSIBLE tells a reader the opposite of the thing that drives urgent treatment. Reserve IRREVERSIBLE for entries where the defining deficiency lesion does not recover at all, such as B12 subacute combined degeneration or the fetal neurodevelopmental injury of maternal iodine deficiency.

chk.coverage: CLEAN. All 7 assigned names present exactly once, no duplicates, no unassigned extras: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol); Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d; Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU; Beta-carotene supplements; Vitamin K2 (MK-7 and MK-4); Cod liver oil; Multivitamin / multimineral.
chk.net:
One misclassification that a reader would act on, one arithmetic error, four sourcing imprecisions. No invented deficiencies in this group.

Priority 1 (invented deficiencies): clean. No botanicals or non-essential compounds are classified CLINICAL or FUNCTIONAL. Beta-carotene is correctly NONE with a well-argued justification (no human process depends on the intact molecule, every requirement it meets is a vitamin A requirement). Cod liver oil and multivitamin are correctly NA as product categories rather than being given borrowed deficiency states. Vitamin K2 as CLINICAL survives scrutiny: menaquinones are vitamin K and directly serve as the gamma-glutamyl carboxylase cofactor, so unlike beta-carotene they are the vitamin rather than a precursor, and the entry states explicitly that no separate K2 requirement exists and that recommendations are set on phylloquinone. Correct call, correctly caveated.

Priority 2 (reversibility): one wrong, the vitamin A IRREVERSIBLE label, detailed above. The other three PARTIAL calls are right and their notes are unusually precise about which components recover. Vitamin D correctly separates biochemistry and myopathy (reverse) from established bowing and pelvic deformity (persist). Vitamin E correctly identifies the early-treatment window and says treatment prevents more than it restores. Vitamin K correctly separates the coagulopathy, which corrects within hours, from haemorrhagic brain injury already sustained.

Priority 3 (dietary versus genetic): handled correctly in the prose. The vitamin E entry explicitly quarantines AVED as a TTPA transport defect rather than a dietary deficiency, and repeats the point under at_risk. The weakness is in the citation rather than the classification: the only clinical reference attached to the entry is an AVED case report.

Priority 4 (overstated severity and unsupported numbers): the vitamin E 400 IU multiple is the only outright wrong number. Everything else checked out against source. NHANES 25(OH)D percentages match Herrick 2019 exactly, including the race breakdown. WHO vitamin A figures match the 2009 report (190 million preschool children, one-third of the at-risk age group, 19.1 million pregnant women, 5.2 million with night blindness). The claim that roughly half of children blinded by vitamin A deficiency die within twelve months is the standard WHO/Sommer figure and is supported. ATBC and CARET effect sizes are accurate. USPSTF 2022 grades are right (D for beta-carotene and vitamin E, I for multivitamins). The cod liver oil history claim is supported by Rajakumar 2003, which frames rickets as rampant in industrialised polluted northern cities with cod liver oil making treatment and eradication possible by the 1930s. VKDB incidence figures are correct in substance and only loosely attributed. Nothing in the group is inflated in the alarmist direction; the vitamin E prevalence field is a model of restraint in refusing to convert the 90 percent below-EAR intake statistic into a deficiency rate.

One gap worth noting rather than scoring as an error: the beta-carotene entry carries its harm signal (ATBC, CARET) inside at_risk, but the vitamin E 400 IU entry cites only the USPSTF D recommendation and omits SELECT, where 400 IU/d alpha-tocopherol raised prostate cancer incidence in healthy men (HR 1.17). Given that the entry is explicitly about the 400 IU dose and that the parallel entry does carry its trial harms, the asymmetry is worth closing.

items.function_short_zh: 促进肠道吸收钙和磷,使骨骼能够正常矿化。
items.function_full_zh: 胆钙化醇(cholecalciferol)先在肝脏羟化为25-羟维生素D,即血液检测中测量的循环储存形式,再在肾脏羟化为1,25-二羟维生素D(骨化三醇,calcitriol),后者是通过核内维生素D受体发挥作用的类固醇激素。骨化三醇驱动肠道对钙和磷的主动吸收,抑制甲状旁腺激素,并维持成骨细胞使新沉积类骨质矿化所需的钙磷乘积。维生素D受体存在于免疫细胞、肌肉及许多其他组织中,但唯一有明确人体需求量的作用是钙与骨代谢这一轴。皮肤经UVB合成通常提供其中大部分,这也是膳食需求量因纬度、季节和日晒而有很大差异的原因。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 生长期儿童表现为佝偻病(rickets),成人表现为骨软化症(osteomalacia)。婴儿严重缺乏还会导致低钙惊厥和扩张型心肌病。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血清25(OH)D先下降,随后甲状旁腺激素升高(继发性甲状旁腺功能亢进),此时血钙仍正常或处于正常低值。这一阶段患者几乎没有察觉:髋部、肋骨和胫骨隐隐作痛,近端肌无力表现为从矮椅上起身或爬楼梯困难。在X线出现任何改变之前,血液检查即可显示25(OH)D偏低、PTH升高,常伴碱性磷酸酶升高。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 儿童期生长板矿化失败,表现为膝内翻或膝外翻、腕踝增宽、肋软骨连接处的佝偻病串珠(rachitic rosary)、学步延迟、生长迟缓及骨折。婴儿可首先表现为低钙性手足搐搦、惊厥或扩张型心肌病,可致命。成人则表现为未矿化类骨质堆积形成的骨软化症,出现骨痛、近端肌病伴摇摆步态,以及Looser带(假性骨折),可进展为耻骨支、股骨颈或肋骨的完全性骨折。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 生化指标、骨痛、肌病、低钙惊厥以及活动性佝偻病的影像学表现,在补充维生素D及足量钙后可完全恢复,通常需数周到数月。但长期佝偻病已形成的骨骼畸形往往持续存在,明显的骨弯曲、佝偻病性侏儒或骨盆畸形可能需要手术矫正。
items.at_risk_zh: 有效日晒不足者:长期居家或住养老机构的老年人、皮肤全遮盖者,以及冬季生活在高纬度地区的人群。高纬度地区肤色较深者(黑色素越多,UVB合成越少)。未额外补充维生素D的纯母乳喂养婴儿,因为母乳中维生素D含量低。肥胖者(维生素D被脂肪组织截留)。乳糜泻、囊性纤维化、胆汁淤积或减重手术导致的脂肪吸收不良者。慢性肾病或肝病患者,以及长期使用抗惊厥药或糖皮质激素治疗者。
items.prevalence_zh: NHANES 2011-2014年数据:美国1岁及以上人群中,5.0%血清25(OH)D低于30 nmol/L(处于缺乏风险),18.3%处于30至49.9 nmol/L之间;低于30 nmol/L的比例在非西班牙裔黑人中为17.5%,而非西班牙裔白人中仅为2.1%(PMID 31076739)。临床营养性佝偻病在高收入国家并不常见但并未消失,在中东、非洲和南亚部分地区仍然常见(PMID 26741135)。

items.supplement: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
items.function_short_zh: 人体主要的脂溶性抗氧化剂,保护细胞膜和神经免受氧化损伤。
items.function_full_zh: α-生育酚(alpha-tocopherol)是人体唯一保留的维生素E形式。吸收后,肝脏的α-生育酚转运蛋白(alpha-tocopherol transfer protein, TTPA)选择性地将α-生育酚装载到VLDL上运往各组织,而其他生育酚及生育三烯酚则被代谢并排出体外。其确立的功能是阻断细胞膜和脂蛋白中多不饱和脂肪酸的脂质过氧化连锁反应,向脂质过氧自由基提供一个氢原子,随后由抗坏血酸使其再生。缺乏时最先受累的组织是周围神经轴突、脊髓后索和小脑、视网膜以及红细胞膜。400 IU的剂量约为成人每日15 mg RDA的12至18倍,具体倍数取决于产品是合成型还是天然来源型,因此在此剂量下已属药理性使用,而非纠正膳食摄入不足。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 没有单一的经典病名。公认的综合征是维生素E缺乏性共济失调,一种伴周围神经病变和色素性视网膜病变的脊髓小脑变性;在早产儿中则表现为早产儿溶血性贫血。孤立性维生素E缺乏性共济失调(ataxia with isolated vitamin E deficiency, AVED)临床表现相同,但属于遗传性TTPA基因缺陷,并非膳食缺乏。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血浆α-生育酚低于约12 micromol/L,或生育酚与总脂质比值偏低,通常先于症状出现数月至数年,是实用的检测指标。最早的临床体征是踝反射消失、足部振动觉和关节位置觉减退,有时伴暗处行走不稳。早产儿则表现为网织红细胞升高的溶血性贫血。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 未经治疗会进展为脊髓小脑合并感觉障碍的表现:后索变性导致的共济失调、构音障碍、眼肌麻痹、头部震颤、近端肌无力,以及伴视力下降的色素性视网膜病变。终末状态是患者无法独立行走,遗留固定性感觉性共济失调和神经病变。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 大剂量补充能可靠地阻止病情进展,若及早开始治疗(症状出现后约一年内,或在已知吸收不良的儿童出现症状之前),大部分神经病变可以恢复。长期存在的后索和小脑变性以及已形成的视网膜病变通常无法完全消退,因此治疗预防的作用大于逆转的作用。
items.at_risk_zh: 几乎仅见于脂肪吸收障碍者:囊性纤维化、胆汁淤积性肝病及胆道闭锁、短肠综合征、慢性胰腺炎、无β脂蛋白血症及纯合子低β脂蛋白血症。早产儿及极低出生体重儿。另外还有遗传性TTPA缺陷(AVED)患者,这属于遗传性转运障碍,而非饮食所致。对于脂肪吸收正常的成人,维生素E摄入不足本身基本不会导致临床缺乏。
items.prevalence_zh: 对于明确的临床缺乏,无确切数据,因为在普通人群中极为罕见,不存在有意义的患病率数字。广为引用的说法称超过90%的美国人α-生育酚摄入未达到平均需要量估算值,这只是摄入量统计,并非缺乏率,也未伴随相应的神经系统疾病负担(doi:10.3945/an.114.006254)。生化意义上的缺乏在未经治疗的囊性纤维化和胆汁淤积性肝病患者中较为常见。

items.supplement: Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU
items.function_short_zh: 生成眼睛在暗光下感光所需的色素,并维持皮肤、肠道和呼吸道黏膜的健康。
items.function_full_zh: 视黄醇(retinol)被氧化为11-顺式视黄醛,后者与视蛋白结合形成视紫红质,即视杆细胞的感光色素,使暗光下视觉成为可能。经另一条途径,视黄醇被氧化为全反式和9-顺式视黄酸,二者是核内RAR和RXR受体的配体,调控上皮分化(结膜、角膜、呼吸道和肠道中杯状细胞及黏蛋白生成)、胚胎模式形成、造血,以及包括T淋巴细胞归巢肠道在内的固有和适应性免疫相关基因的转录。来自肝脏、乳制品、鸡蛋及补充剂的预成视黄醇吸收效率高,储存于肝星状细胞中,可将血浆浓度缓冲达数月之久。10,000 IU约相当于3,000 micrograms视黄醇活性当量,约为成人RDA的四倍,处于可耐受最高摄入量水平,因此在此剂量下临床相关的问题是过量而非不足。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 干眼病(xerophthalmia),病谱从夜盲症(nyctalopia)经结膜和角膜干燥,发展到角膜软化症(keratomalacia)。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 先出现暗适应受损,继而发展为明显的夜盲:黄昏后或光线昏暗的房间中视物困难,幼儿则表现为天黑后不愿走动。随后出现结膜干燥及Bitot斑,即结膜上角化形成的泡沫状灰白色三角形斑块。麻疹、腹泻和呼吸道感染的严重程度及病程延长往往先于任何眼部体征出现。血清视黄醇低于0.70 micromol/L是生化指标,但只有在肝脏储备大量耗竭后才会下降。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 角膜干燥进展为点状角膜病变,继而角膜溃疡,再发展为角膜软化症,角膜基质在数天内液化,常并发穿孔。眼球结构遭到破坏,失明为永久性。缺乏还会显著提高麻疹、腹泻性疾病和呼吸道感染导致的儿童死亡率,因缺乏而致盲的儿童中约有一半会在十二个月内死亡。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 夜盲、结膜干燥和Bitot斑在给予大剂量视黄醇后数天到数周内可以逆转。一旦角膜发生溃疡或软化,损害即为结构性且永久,维生素A缺乏至今仍是全球儿童可预防性失明的主要原因之一。对于病重、储备耗竭的患儿,从完全可逆阶段到不可逆阶段之间的窗口期可能仅有数天,这正是临床一旦怀疑即予治疗、无需等待视黄醇检测结果的原因。
items.at_risk_zh: 低收入地区饮食中动物性食物或维生素A原蔬菜摄入不足的学龄前儿童及孕期、哺乳期妇女,尤其是麻疹和腹泻性疾病常见的地区。在高收入国家,缺乏较为罕见,几乎总是继发于疾病:囊性纤维化、胆汁淤积性肝病、短肠综合征、胰腺功能不全及减重手术。极端限制性饮食也可导致缺乏,包括部分自闭症儿童中出现的食物选择性进食,已有相关干眼病病例报告。
items.prevalence_zh: WHO估计,1995至2005年间,全球有1.9亿学龄前儿童(占高风险人群中该年龄组的33.3%)及1,910万孕妇血清视黄醇低于0.70 micromol/L,其中约520万学龄前儿童患有夜盲症(WHO, Global prevalence of vitamin A deficiency in populations at risk 1995-2005, Geneva 2009)。高收入人群中的缺乏较为罕见,且多与疾病相关而非饮食所致;这些地区没有具有实际意义的人群患病率数据。

items.function_short_zh: 一种植物色素,人体可将其转化为维生素A;人体没有任何过程直接需要它本身。
items.function_full_zh: β-胡萝卜素是一种维生素A原类胡萝卜素,是胡萝卜、红薯、南瓜及深绿色叶菜中的橙色色素。在肠黏膜中,β-胡萝卜素15,15'-加氧酶(beta-carotene 15,15'-oxygenase, BCO1)将其裂解为视黄醛,后者被还原为视黄醇并酯化储存。这一转化受反馈调节且效率不高:美国医学研究所(Institute of Medicine)将12 micrograms膳食β-胡萝卜素的维生素A活性定为等同于1 microgram视黄醇(补充剂形式的油溶β-胡萝卜素为2 micrograms,因为经纯化的油基β-胡萝卜素绕过了食物基质释放这一步骤),而常见的BCO1基因变异会使相当一部分人的转化效率显著降低。未被裂解的β-胡萝卜素在实验系统中可作为脂相抗氧化剂和单线态氧猝灭剂,但人体没有任何生理过程依赖完整分子本身,它所能满足的一切需求,都是预成视黄醇可以直接满足的维生素A需求。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。没有人会出现β-胡萝卜素缺乏。只要供给预成维生素A,完全不含β-胡萝卜素的饮食在营养上仍然是完整的。对于这一化合物,临床上确立的效应方向是补充剂量下的危害,而非任何缺乏风险:在ATBC试验(单用β-胡萝卜素20 mg/d)和CARET试验(β-胡萝卜素30 mg/d联合视黄醇)中,补充使吸烟者和石棉暴露工人的肺癌发生率及总死亡率升高(PMID 8127329, PMID 8602180)。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用,因为不存在缺乏状态。血浆类胡萝卜素浓度低是蔬菜摄入不足的有用指标,而非缺乏症的诊断依据,也没有明确的临床阈值。

items.function_short_zh: 激活参与血液凝固以及引导钙沉积入骨骼而非动脉壁的蛋白质。
items.function_full_zh: 所有形式的维生素K都作为γ-谷氨酰羧化酶(gamma-glutamyl carboxylase)的辅因子发挥作用,该酶将特定的谷氨酸残基转化为γ-羧基谷氨酸(Gla),使相应蛋白质获得结合钙并发挥功能的能力。在肝脏中,这一反应激活凝血因子II、VII、IX和X,以及抗凝蛋白C、S和Z,膳食需求量正是依据这一功能设定的。在肝脏之外,同一反应激活骨内的骨钙素(osteocalcin)和血管平滑肌内的基质Gla蛋白(matrix Gla protein),后者是动脉钙化的局部抑制因子。MK-7与叶绿醌(phylloquinone, K1)的主要区别在于药代动力学:较长的类异戊二烯侧链使其循环半衰期以天计而非以小时计,因而能更持续地到达肝外组织。MK-4则是组织自身经UBIAD1从K1或甲萘醌转化合成的形式,作为补充剂时数小时内即被清除。提高甲萘醌类摄入量,超过维持正常羧化所需的量,是否会改变骨骼或血管方面的结局,这属于关于补充剂使用的问题,与该维生素本身的必需作用是两回事。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 维生素K缺乏性出血(vitamin K deficiency bleeding, VKDB),旧称新生儿出血症。没有专门归因于甲萘醌类的缺乏病:摄入建议是针对总维生素K设定的,并以叶绿醌为基础,尚未确立单独的K2需求量。
items.deficiency_early_zh: PIVKA-II(羧化不足的凝血酶原)升高是最早的凝血指标,随后出现凝血酶原时间延长和INR升高。临床表现为易出现瘀伤、穿刺或静脉穿刺部位渗血、鼻出血、牙龈出血或月经量增多。羧化不足的骨钙素会在任何凝血指标之前升高,但单独而言,这只是一项生化发现,其临床意义尚不明确。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 在新生儿中,经典型VKDB出现在出生后第一周,表现为脐残端、胃肠道、包皮环切部位或穿刺伤口出血。迟发型VKDB出现在出生后2至12周,是危险的类型:约半数病例表现为颅内出血,导致死亡或永久性神经损伤。在存在严重吸收不良、胆汁淤积,或长期使用广谱抗生素合并摄入不足的成人中,缺乏可导致自发性胃肠道、腹膜后或颅内出血。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 凝血功能障碍本身可以完全且迅速纠正:肠外途径给予维生素K可在数小时内恢复凝血因子活性,凝血酶原复合物浓缩剂则可立即起效。无法逆转的是已经发生的出血所造成的损伤,迟发型VKDB的颅内出血会使相当比例的患儿遗留永久性神经系统损害或死亡。这正是出生时预防比事后治疗更为重要的原因。
items.at_risk_zh: 首要风险人群是新生儿,他们出生时储备低,母乳中维生素K含量少,肠道菌群也尚未成熟。出生时肌注维生素K可预防这一情况,如今在高收入国家,拒绝或漏打这一针剂是迟发型VKDB的主要原因。婴儿期之后:脂肪吸收不良、胆汁淤积及胆道梗阻、囊性纤维化、大范围小肠切除者,以及使用华法林等维生素K拮抗剂的人群,这类人群的缺乏是被有意诱导的。健康成人的膳食性维生素K缺乏较为罕见,因为叶绿醌在绿叶蔬菜中含量丰富,且肝脏能有效地将其循环利用。
items.prevalence_zh: 在未预防的情况下,欧洲监测系列数据显示迟发型VKDB发生率约为每10万出生4至7例(PMID 18804903),东南亚报告的发生率显著更高;据CDC/AAP估计,迟发型VKDB约为每10万出生4.4至7.2例,经典型VKDB则影响约0.25%至1.7%的未预防新生儿。健康成人中临床维生素K缺乏罕见,尚无确立的人群患病率数据。相当一部分成人体内可检测到羧化不足的骨钙素和失活的基质Gla蛋白,但这只是一项生物标志物观察,并无明确的临床缺乏阈值。

items.function_short_zh: 一种鱼肝油,同时提供维生素D、预成维生素A和omega-3脂肪酸。
items.function_full_zh: 鱼肝油是一种食品,由鳕形目(Gadus)鱼类的肝脏炼制而成,一次服用即同时含有三种活性成分:维生素D3、以视黄酯形式存在的预成维生素A,以及长链omega-3脂肪酸EPA和DHA。每种成分各有其自身的生理机制(参见维生素D3和预成维生素A条目;EPA和DHA被整合入膜磷脂,并作为类花生酸及特化促消退介质的前体,DHA在视网膜感光细胞和神经元膜中富集)。鱼肝油具有历史地位,因为在维生素D本身被发现之前,它是二十世纪初在污染严重的工业城市中治疗并最终基本消除佝偻病的手段。现代产品的含量差异很大,取决于精炼过程中天然维生素是否被去除后又重新添加,因此标签内容很重要。剂量方面实际的限制因素是预成视黄醇:摄入量若大到足以提供有意义的EPA和DHA量,可能使维生素A摄入接近或超过可耐受最高摄入量,而这里的维生素A是视黄醇,不是β-胡萝卜素。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。鱼肝油是一个产品类别,而非营养素本身。相关的缺乏状态属于其各组成成分,已在维生素D3和预成维生素A条目中描述。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。没有人会缺乏鱼肝油本身。缺乏风险归属于其各组成营养素,主要是维生素D,已在该条目中列出。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用,属于产品类别而非营养素。

items.function_short_zh: 同时提供多种营养素的低剂量混合补充;它本身没有独立的功能。
items.function_full_zh: 复合维生素/矿物质是一个产品类别,而非单一物质:通常是每日一剂的固定组合,提供大致相当于RDA的十到三十种维生素和矿物质。它本身没有独立的生理机制,其在体内的作用不过是各单一营养素作用的总和,每种营养素通过各自的途径发挥效应。不同配方在所含营养素种类、化学形式(铁为硫酸盐还是双甘氨酸螯合物,叶酸为叶酸还是5-MTHF,维生素D为D2还是D3)以及占RDA的比例或倍数上差异极大,因此某一产品的试验证据很难推广到另一产品上。它合理的用途是作为膳食不足时的一种保障。已确诊的缺乏症需以治疗剂量的特定营养素进行治疗,这不是复合维生素所能提供的。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。不存在复合维生素缺乏状态。复合维生素可能有实际用处的人群是那些摄入确实受限的人:总体进食量很少的老年人、采取限制性或消除性饮食的人、存在吸收不良的人,以及减重手术后的患者(这类患者需要专门的高剂量方案,并单独监测B12、铁和脂溶性维生素,而非笼统的复合维生素)。在妊娠期,证据基础是叶酸和碘这两种具体营养素,不涵盖复合维生素整体。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用,属于产品类别而非营养素。关于在总体健康、非妊娠成人中预防心血管疾病或癌症,USPSTF在2022年的结论是证据不足以评估获益与危害的平衡(I级声明)。

items: High-dose folic acid plus B12 for cardiovascular prevention

items.function_short: Supplies the one-carbon units cells need to build DNA and divide.
items.function_full: Folate is reduced to tetrahydrofolate, which carries one-carbon groups for thymidylate and purine synthesis and for the remethylation of homocysteine to methionine by methionine synthase (a B12-dependent enzyme). Tissues that divide fastest depend on it most: bone marrow, gut mucosa, and the closing neural tube of an early embryo. Folic acid is the synthetic, fully oxidised form; it must be reduced by dihydrofolate reductase, whose capacity in humans is limited, so unmetabolised folic acid appears in plasma at intakes above roughly 200 to 400 micrograms in one dose. The natural circulating form is 5-methyltetrahydrofolate.
items.deficiency_name: Megaloblastic (macrocytic) anaemia. In early pregnancy, folate deficiency causes neural tube defects: anencephaly, spina bifida, encephalocele.
items.deficiency_early: Serum folate falls first, then red cell folate. Raised mean corpuscular volume appears before anaemia, with hypersegmented neutrophils on the film. Symptoms are non-specific: tiredness, breathlessness on exertion, sore tongue, mouth ulcers, mild diarrhoea. In pregnancy there are no maternal warning signs at all; the first evidence of a neural tube defect is usually the anomaly scan.
items.deficiency_severe: Marrow failure with pancytopenia, severe anaemia, mucosal ulceration and malabsorptive diarrhoea. In pregnancy the severe endpoint is structural: anencephaly is incompatible with life, and open spina bifida causes lifelong paralysis below the lesion, hydrocephalus, and bowel and bladder impairment.
items.reversibility_note: The haematological and mucosal effects reverse completely: reticulocytosis begins within a week and the blood count normalises in about two months, with no residual deficit. A neural tube defect that has already formed is permanent and cannot be reversed by any later intake. The neural tube closes 26 to 28 days after conception, so supplementation started after a positive pregnancy test is too late for that specific endpoint, which is the whole argument for taking it before conception.
items.at_risk: Women who could become pregnant, particularly with an unplanned pregnancy. Coeliac disease and other malabsorption. Heavy alcohol use. Drugs that block folate handling: methotrexate, sulfasalazine, trimethoprim, phenytoin and other anticonvulsants. High-turnover states such as chronic haemolysis and exfoliative skin disease. Dialysis.
items.prevalence: In the fortified United States, 18.6% of women aged 12 to 49 had red cell folate below the threshold associated with elevated neural tube defect risk (748 nmol/L) in 2011 to 2016, down from 23.2% in 2007 to 2010 (PMID 31504109). Frank folate-deficiency anaemia is now uncommon where fortification is mandatory and remains common where it is not.
items.source: PMID 31504109 (Pfeiffer et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2019, US folate status 20 years after fortification); PMID 1677062 (MRC Vitamin Study, Lancet 1991: 4 mg/day periconceptional folic acid cut neural tube defect recurrence by 72%, RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.71)

items.function_short: Needed by two enzymes: one for making new blood cells, one for nerve insulation.
items.function_full: Cobalamin is the cofactor for exactly two human enzymes. Methionine synthase remethylates homocysteine to methionine using 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, which both regenerates usable folate and supplies S-adenosylmethionine for the methylation reactions that maintain myelin. Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase converts methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA in the mitochondrion during breakdown of odd-chain fatty acids and branched-chain amino acids. Absorption is elaborate: gastric acid and pepsin release B12 from food protein, intrinsic factor from parietal cells carries it, and receptors in the terminal ileum take it up. Outside vegan diets the usual cause of deficiency is failure somewhere along that route rather than low intake.
items.deficiency_name: Pernicious anaemia (autoimmune intrinsic factor failure) and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord; megaloblastic anaemia is the haematological presentation.
items.deficiency_early: Methylmalonic acid and homocysteine rise before serum B12 drops into the clearly deficient range, which is why borderline results are often followed with those metabolites. Symmetrical tingling and numbness in the feet and hands, loss of vibration sense and joint position sense, unsteadiness that is worse in the dark. Macrocytosis with hypersegmented neutrophils, sore smooth tongue, fatigue, mild cognitive slowing and low mood. Neurological signs can be present with a completely normal full blood count.
items.deficiency_severe: Subacute combined degeneration: demyelination of the dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts producing sensory ataxia, spasticity, extensor plantar responses, and bladder and bowel disturbance, progressing untreated to spastic paraparesis and loss of independent walking. Optic atrophy occurs in a minority, as do dementia and psychosis. Severe megaloblastic anaemia with pancytopenia can occur, but it is the neurology that disables.
items.reversibility_note: The blood corrects fully (reticulocytosis within a week, counts normal in roughly eight weeks) while the neurology may not. Recovery is fastest in the first two months and continues to about six months; deficits that have been present for six to twelve months or more often leave permanent sensory ataxia, spasticity or bladder impairment, and the degree of disability before treatment predicts what remains after it. This split is exactly why folate must not be given blind for an unexplained macrocytic anaemia: folic acid repairs the blood picture and removes the visible signal while the cord damage carries on.
items.at_risk: Adults over 60 with atrophic gastritis and food-bound B12 malabsorption. Autoimmune pernicious anaemia. Gastrectomy or gastric bypass, ileal resection, Crohn's disease. Long-term metformin. Long-term proton pump inhibitors or H2 blockers. Strict vegans and, importantly, their exclusively breastfed infants. Repeated nitrous oxide exposure, recreational or occupational, which inactivates methionine synthase directly.
items.prevalence: About 6% of people aged 60 and over in large US and UK surveys have plasma B12 below 148 pmol/L, and close to 20% are in the marginal range of 148 to 221 pmol/L; prevalence rises with age and is considerably higher in low-income countries across the whole life span (PMID 19116323).
items.source: PMID 19116323 (Allen, Am J Clin Nutr 2009, How common is vitamin B-12 deficiency?); PMID 1648656 (Healton et al., Medicine 1991, 153 episodes of neurological cobalamin deficiency; residual deficit predicted by severity and duration before treatment)

items.function_short: Vitamin B6 powers amino acid enzymes; at high doses it damages sensory nerves.
items.function_full: The active form, pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, is the cofactor for well over 100 enzymes, most of them in amino acid metabolism: transaminases, the decarboxylases that make serotonin, dopamine, GABA and histamine, the first committed step of haem synthesis (ALA synthase), glycogen phosphorylase, and cystathionine beta-synthase and gamma-lyase, which dispose of homocysteine by transsulphuration. Requirement rises with protein intake. Above the point where these enzymes are saturated, extra B6 adds no function. High-dose products (typically 50 to 500 mg/day, sold for premenstrual symptoms, carpal tunnel syndrome, nausea in pregnancy, or hidden inside B-complex and energy formulations) instead produce a dose-dependent and duration-dependent sensory neuropathy, with the dorsal root ganglion as the target.
items.deficiency_early: Plasma pyridoxal 5'-phosphate below about 20 nmol/L, usually with no symptoms at all. When symptoms appear they are mucocutaneous and non-specific: angular cheilitis, glossitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis around the eyes, nose and mouth, plus irritability and low mood. Homocysteine may be mildly raised.
items.deficiency_severe: Microcytic sideroblastic anaemia from impaired haem synthesis, and a peripheral sensory neuropathy. In infants, deficiency causes seizures through failure of GABA synthesis. Isolated severe deficiency is rare and is nearly always secondary: isoniazid, cycloserine, hydralazine or penicillamine treatment, alcohol dependence, dialysis, or malabsorption. Note that both deficiency and excess of B6 produce peripheral neuropathy, so neuropathy in a supplement user is at least as likely to be caused by the supplement as corrected by it.
items.reversibility_note: Deficiency itself corrects fully within weeks on modest repletion. The partial rating belongs to the excess: the sensory neuropathy caused by high-dose B6 usually improves over several months after the supplement is stopped, sometimes substantially, but residual numbness and impaired position sense persist in some people because the injury is to the sensory nerve cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglion rather than to the axon alone. Onset is inversely related to dose, so grams per day can do it in weeks while tens of milligrams may take years.
items.at_risk: For deficiency: people taking isoniazid, cycloserine, hydralazine or penicillamine; alcohol dependence; dialysis; malabsorption. Lower plasma PLP is also seen in older adults, smokers, and current or former oral contraceptive users. For toxicity: anyone taking a high-dose B6 or B-complex product for months to years, often without realising the dose, since a single tablet can exceed the European upper level several-fold.
items.prevalence: Around 23 to 27% of US adults not taking supplements had plasma PLP below 20 nmol/L in NHANES 2003 to 2004, mostly biochemical rather than symptomatic (PMID 18469270). On the toxicity side, EFSA set the adult tolerable upper intake at 12 mg/day in 2023, derived from a 50 mg/day reference point for peripheral neuropathy with an uncertainty factor of 4 (doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006).
items.source: PMID 18469270 (Morris et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2008, plasma PLP in NHANES 2003 to 2004); PMID 6308447 (Schaumburg et al., N Engl J Med 1983, sensory neuropathy from pyridoxine abuse); doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006 (EFSA 2023, tolerable upper intake level for vitamin B6)

items.function_short: Keeps collagen strong and wounds healing; without it blood vessels and gums break down.
items.function_full: Ascorbate is the reducing cofactor that keeps the iron atom in a family of dioxygenases in its active state. The best known are prolyl-4-hydroxylase and lysyl hydroxylase, which hydroxylate collagen so the triple helix is stable and can be cross-linked; without them the collagen laid down is defective, which explains bleeding, poor wound healing and the reopening of old scars. The same chemistry serves dopamine beta-hydroxylase (noradrenaline synthesis), peptidylglycine alpha-amidating monooxygenase (peptide hormone amidation), two carnitine biosynthesis enzymes, and the HIF prolyl hydroxylases and TET and JmjC demethylases in gene regulation. Ascorbate also reduces dietary non-haem iron to the absorbable ferrous form. Humans cannot synthesise it because the gulonolactone oxidase gene is inactive.
items.deficiency_early: After roughly one to three months of intake below about 10 mg/day, plasma ascorbate falls and body stores drop under about 300 mg. The first phase is fatigue, irritability and diffuse aching in the legs, with nothing visible. Then come the specific skin signs: perifollicular hyperkeratosis with corkscrew-shaped body hairs on the thighs and shins, perifollicular haemorrhage, easy bruising, and swollen, spongy, bleeding gums in anyone who still has teeth.
items.deficiency_severe: Bleeding into skin, muscle and joints, haemarthrosis, and subperiosteal haemorrhage, which in children causes severe limb pain and refusal to move (pseudoparalysis). Old wounds and scars break down, teeth loosen and are lost, anaemia and oedema develop. Untreated scurvy is fatal, usually from haemorrhage or cardiac failure, though it very rarely reaches that stage in current practice because treatment is trivially available.
items.reversibility_note: Complete and unusually fast. Fatigue and pain begin improving within 24 to 48 hours of treatment, bleeding gums and bruising settle over one to two weeks, and full recovery takes around three months on 100 to 300 mg/day. No permanent deficit remains. The only exception is teeth already lost, which do not grow back.
items.at_risk: People whose diets contain almost no fruit or vegetables: highly restrictive or selective eaters including some autistic children, people living alone with severe mental illness or dementia, alcohol and drug dependence, homelessness and food insecurity. Also smokers (requirement about 35 mg/day higher), people on dialysis, malabsorption, and some patients after bariatric surgery. Scurvy is a disease of dietary pattern, not of insufficient supplementation; roughly 10 mg/day prevents it and a single orange comfortably exceeds that.
items.prevalence: 7.1% (SE 0.9) of the US population aged 6 and over had serum ascorbate below 11.4 micromol/L in NHANES 2003 to 2004, down from about 13% in NHANES III, with the highest rates in smokers and low-income groups (PMID 19675106).
items.source: PMID 19675106 (Schleicher et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2009, serum vitamin C and prevalence of deficiency in the United States, NHANES 2003 to 2004)

items.supplement: High-dose folic acid plus B12 for cardiovascular prevention
items.function_short: Lowers homocysteine in the blood, which turns out not to prevent heart attacks.
items.function_full: Folic acid with B12, often with B6 added, reliably lowers plasma total homocysteine by roughly a quarter, because both vitamins feed the methionine synthase step that converts homocysteine back to methionine. The rationale was observational: raised homocysteine tracks with vascular disease and stroke. Randomised trials separated the biomarker from the disease. Pooling 15 trials and 71,422 participants, homocysteine lowering had no effect on myocardial infarction (7.1% versus 6.0%, RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.10) or death from any cause (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.06), with a small reduction in stroke (4.3% versus 5.1%, RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82 to 0.99) driven largely by trials in populations without folic acid fortification and with low baseline folate. One safety point carries over from the components: high-dose folic acid given without first checking B12 status can normalise the anaemia of B12 deficiency while the spinal cord damage continues undetected, so B12 status should be established before folate is given at these doses.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. This is a therapeutic regimen tested for cardiovascular prevention, not a nutrient. The deficiency states of the two components are covered in their own entries.
items.deficiency_severe: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no deficiency of a combination product.
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. No deficiency state exists for an intervention category.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. No deficiency state exists for an intervention category.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE. For scale of effect rather than deficiency: the Cochrane estimate is that roughly 143 people would need treating for 5.4 years to prevent one stroke, in the trial setting where the stroke signal appeared (PMID 28816346).
items.source: PMID 28816346 (Marti-Carvajal et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2017, homocysteine-lowering interventions for preventing cardiovascular events, 15 trials, 71,422 participants)

errors.correction: "In early pregnancy, folate deficiency causes neural tube defects" states a deterministic cause for what is a probabilistic risk factor. Low maternal folate raises NTD risk along a continuous dose-response curve, and periconceptional folic acid prevents a large share of NTDs (72% recurrence reduction, MRC 1991), but most NTD pregnancies occur in women who are not frankly folate deficient, and a residual fraction of NTDs is not folate-responsive at all. Rewrite as: "low folate status raises the risk of neural tube defects (anencephaly, spina bifida, encephalocele); periconceptional folic acid prevents a large proportion but not all of them." The rest of the entry already handles this correctly, so this is a wording defect in the one field a reader scans first.
errors.source: PMID 1677062 (MRC Vitamin Study 1991, RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.71, verified verbatim); Daly et al. JAMA 1995 continuous RBC-folate/NTD dose-response; USPSTF folic acid evidence review (NBK593617), which notes prevention occurs even in women with normal folate concentrations

errors.supplement: High-dose folic acid plus B12 for cardiovascular prevention
errors.field: function_full (trial counts attached to outcome estimates)
errors.correction: "Pooling 15 trials and 71,422 participants, homocysteine lowering had no effect on myocardial infarction..." attaches the whole-review denominator to each outcome. In the Cochrane review, 15 trials / 71,422 participants is the total included; the MI estimate (7.1% vs 6.0%, RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.10) comes from 12 trials / 46,699 participants, stroke (4.3% vs 5.1%, RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82 to 0.99) from 10 trials / 44,224, and all-cause death (11.7% vs 12.3%, RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.06) from 11 trials / 44,817. Every effect estimate and percentage in the entry is correct; only the denominator attribution is not. Also add the all-cause-death percentages, which are currently dropped while MI and stroke keep theirs.
errors.source: PMID 28816346 (Marti-Carvajal et al., Cochrane 2017), abstract verified verbatim

errors.correction: "Deficits that have been present for six to twelve months or more often leave permanent sensory ataxia, spasticity or bladder impairment" runs ahead of the cited source. Healton 1991 (153 episodes in 143 patients) reported complete resolution of neurologic abnormalities in 47.1% and residual moderate-to-severe disability in only 6.3%; what the paper establishes is that the extent of residual deficit is inversely related to pre-treatment severity and symptom duration. The IRREVERSIBLE classification is correct and should stand, but the note should carry the numbers: most treated patients recover fully or nearly so, a minority are left disabled, and the risk of residual deficit rises with how long the deficiency ran untreated.
errors.source: PMID 1648656 (Healton et al., Medicine 1991), abstract verified: 47.1% complete recovery, 6.3% residual moderate-to-severe disability

errors.supplement: High-dose folic acid plus B12 for cardiovascular prevention
errors.correction: "The Cochrane estimate is that roughly 143 people would need treating for 5.4 years to prevent one stroke" omits both the confidence interval and the specific comparison it belongs to. Cochrane derives NNTB 143 (95% CI 85 to 428) over 5.4 years from the folic acid plus enalapril comparison (the CSPPT trial in an unfortified Chinese hypertensive population), not from the pooled 10-trial stroke estimate. The entry's hedge "in the trial setting where the stroke signal appeared" gestures at this but does not name it. State it: "NNTB 143 (95% CI 85 to 428) over 5.4 years, from the folic acid plus enalapril comparison in an unfortified population."
errors.source: PMID 28816346 (Marti-Carvajal et al., Cochrane 2017), abstract verified verbatim

errors.correction: "Microcytic sideroblastic anaemia from impaired haem synthesis" blurs a nutritional state into a genetic one. Nutritional or drug-induced B6 deficiency produces a hypochromic microcytic anaemia; the classic pyridoxine-responsive sideroblastic anaemia with ring sideroblasts is usually the X-linked ALAS2 disorder, a genetic condition in which pharmacological pyridoxine is treatment rather than repletion. The entry's own drug list (isoniazid, cycloserine, penicillamine) covers the acquired route, so the fix is one clause: "hypochromic microcytic anaemia from impaired haem synthesis (distinct from X-linked ALAS2 pyridoxine-responsive sideroblastic anaemia, which is genetic, not dietary)."
errors.source: NIH ODS Vitamin B6 Health Professional fact sheet (lists microcytic anaemia as the deficiency sign); standard haematology classification of X-linked sideroblastic anaemia (ALAS2) as pyridoxine-responsive

errors.correction: "Frank folate-deficiency anaemia is now uncommon where fortification is mandatory and remains common where it is not" carries no source or number, and the entry's only prevalence citation (PMID 31504109) is a US fortified-population survey that cannot support the unfortified-country half of the sentence. Either cite a figure for an unfortified setting or soften to "and is seen more often where it is not." The fortified-US numbers in the same field are exact and check out.
errors.source: PMID 31504109 (Pfeiffer et al. 2019), abstract verified verbatim: folate insufficiency (RBC folate <748 nmol/L) in women fell from 23.2% (2007 to 2010) to 18.6% (2011 to 2016); the paper contains no unfortified-country comparison

misclassified.why: The reversibility column silently changes meaning on this one row. Every other entry uses it for the deficiency state; here the note openly concedes the switch: "Deficiency itself corrects fully within weeks on modest repletion. The partial rating belongs to the excess." A reader scanning the column, which is the field they would act on, reads "B6 deficiency is only partly reversible", which the entry itself says is false. Set reversibility to FULL for the deficiency and record the high-dose sensory neuronopathy's incomplete recovery in a separate toxicity field. The clinical content about the dorsal root ganglion is accurate and worth keeping (Schaumburg 1983; EFSA 2023 applies an uncertainty factor of 4 to a 50 mg/day reference point precisely because time to onset falls as dose rises), it is just filed under the wrong label. Leaving PARTIAL here also breaks any cross-row comparison: it is the only row whose reversibility describes a harm from taking the supplement rather than a harm from lacking it.

FUNCTIONAL paired with deficiency_name "NONE" is internally contradictory, and it contradicts the row's own text. FUNCTIONAL should mean biochemical change without a named clinical syndrome, yet deficiency_severe describes hypochromic microcytic anaemia, peripheral sensory neuropathy, and infantile seizures from failed GABA synthesis, which is a named clinical deficiency syndrome. B6 is an essential nutrient with a recognised deficiency state, so FUNCTIONAL understates it. Two consistent repairs exist: either set deficiency_state to CLINICAL and fill deficiency_name ("pyridoxine deficiency: seborrhoeic dermatitis with cheilosis and glossitis, hypochromic microcytic anaemia, and seizures in infants; nearly always secondary to isoniazid, cycloserine, hydralazine or penicillamine, alcohol dependence, dialysis or malabsorption"), or treat the row strictly as a dose-defined excess entry and use NA / NONE with the deficiency fields marked NOT APPLICABLE, the convention this dataset already applies to the folic-acid-plus-B12 intervention row. CLINICAL is the better fit because the row does document the deficiency in detail and the sibling naming convention ("Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d", "Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU") shows these high-dose rows still cover the parent nutrient.

chk.coverage: CLEAN. All five assigned names present exactly once: Folic acid; Vitamin B12 (cobalamin); High-dose vitamin B6; Vitamin C; High-dose folic acid plus B12 for cardiovascular prevention. No duplicates, no extras, no unassigned items.
chk.net:
No invented deficiencies in this group. Every item is an essential water-soluble vitamin or a correctly labelled intervention category; the folic-acid-plus-B12 row is properly NA / NONE with all deficiency fields marked NOT APPLICABLE. Nothing here needed downgrading to NONE.

Reversibility is right on the mandated cases: B12 subacute combined degeneration IRREVERSIBLE, scurvy FULL, folate PARTIAL with the split correctly explained (haematology reverses completely, a formed neural tube defect never does, closure at day 26 to 28). Iodine is not in this group. The one reversibility defect is High-dose vitamin B6, and it matters more than a mislabel usually would: the field switches from meaning deficiency-reversibility to toxicity-reversibility on that single row, so a reader comparing rows gets the opposite of what the entry's own note says. That plus its self-contradictory FUNCTIONAL / "NONE" pairing are the two findings worth acting on first.

I verified every quantitative claim against the cited source abstracts, and the numbers themselves are unusually clean. Confirmed verbatim: folate insufficiency 23.2% to 18.6% with the correct downward direction and the 748 nmol/L cutoff (PMID 31504109); MRC 4 mg periconceptional folic acid, 72% protective effect, RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.71 (PMID 1677062); B12 about 6% below 148 pmol/L at 60+ in US and UK surveys with close to 20% marginal at 148 to 221 pmol/L (PMID 19116323); Healton 153 episodes in 143 patients with residual deficit predicted by pre-treatment severity and duration (PMID 1648656); plasma PLP below 20 nmol/L in 23 to 27% of US adult supplement non-users (PMID 18469270); EFSA 2023 UL 12 mg/day from a 50 mg/day reference point with an uncertainty factor of 4 (doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006, which yields 12.5 rounded to 12); vitamin C deficiency 7.1% +/- 0.9 SE at ages 6 and over, down from about 13% in NHANES III (PMID 19675106); and all three Cochrane effect estimates with their event percentages (PMID 28816346). Unmetabolised folic acid appearing above roughly 200 to 400 micrograms per dose also checks out. Every PMID resolves to the paper the entry names.

Dietary-versus-genetic confusion is close to clean. Pernicious anaemia is correctly called autoimmune rather than inherited, and the inactive gulonolactone oxidase gene is correctly presented as a species-wide trait rather than a disorder. The single soft spot is "microcytic sideroblastic anaemia" in the B6 row, where the ring-sideroblast phenotype belongs mostly to X-linked ALAS2 disease; one clause fixes it.

Remaining findings are wording rather than fact: the folate row asserts causation for neural tube defects where the literature supports elevated risk plus large-but-partial preventability, the B12 note says "often leave permanent" deficits where the cited paper reports 47.1% complete recovery and 6.3% moderate-to-severe residual disability, and the Cochrane row attaches the 15-trial / 71,422 denominator to outcome estimates that pooled 10 to 12 trials while dropping the NNTB confidence interval and the CSPPT-specific provenance. Fix the two B6 classifications and the four wording items and this group is sound.

items.function_short_zh: 为细胞合成DNA和分裂提供所需的一碳单位。
items.function_full_zh: 食物叶酸(folate)被还原为四氢叶酸,四氢叶酸携带一碳基团,用于胸苷酸和嘌呤的合成,也用于经methionine synthase(一种依赖维生素B12的酶)将同型半胱氨酸重新甲基化为甲硫氨酸。分裂最快的组织对其依赖最深:骨髓、肠道黏膜,以及早期胚胎正在闭合的神经管。叶酸(folic acid)是人工合成的完全氧化形式,必须经dihydrofolate reductase还原,而人体内该酶的处理能力有限,因此单次摄入量高于约200至400微克时,血浆中就会出现未代谢的叶酸。体内天然循环形式是5-甲基四氢叶酸。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 巨幼细胞性(大细胞性)贫血。在孕早期,叶酸水平偏低会升高神经管缺陷(无脑畸形、脊柱裂、脑膨出)的风险;孕前及孕早期补充叶酸可预防其中大部分,但并非全部。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血清叶酸先下降,随后是红细胞叶酸下降。平均红细胞体积升高出现在贫血之前,血涂片可见中性粒细胞分叶过多。症状没有特异性:疲倦、活动后气促、舌痛、口腔溃疡、轻度腹泻。在妊娠期间,孕妇本身完全没有警示信号;神经管缺陷的最初证据通常来自胎儿畸形筛查超声。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 骨髓衰竭伴全血细胞减少、重度贫血、黏膜溃疡和吸收不良性腹泻。在妊娠期间,严重结局表现为结构性畸形:无脑畸形与生命不相容,开放性脊柱裂会导致病变平面以下的终身瘫痪、脑积水以及肠道和膀胱功能障碍。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 血液学和黏膜方面的影响可完全逆转:网织红细胞增多在一周内开始出现,血细胞计数约在两个月内恢复正常,不留残余损害。但已经形成的神经管缺陷是永久性的,此后任何补充都无法逆转。神经管在受孕后26至28天闭合,因此在妊娠试验呈阳性后才开始补充叶酸,对这一特定结局而言已经太迟,这正是主张在受孕前就开始补充叶酸的全部理由所在。
items.at_risk_zh: 有可能怀孕的女性,尤其是意外妊娠的情况。乳糜泻及其他吸收不良性疾病。大量饮酒。干扰叶酸代谢的药物:甲氨蝶呤、柳氮磺吡啶、甲氧苄啶,以及苯妥英等其他抗惊厥药。细胞更新率高的状态,如慢性溶血和剥脱性皮肤病。透析。
items.prevalence_zh: 在实行叶酸强化的美国,2011至2016年间,12至49岁女性中有18.6%的红细胞叶酸水平低于与神经管缺陷风险升高相关的阈值(748 nmol/L),低于2007至2010年的23.2%(PMID 31504109)。在强制强化的地区,明显的叶酸缺乏性贫血现已不常见;在未强制强化的地区则更为多见。

items.function_short_zh: 两种人体酶依赖它:一种用于制造新血细胞,另一种用于维持神经的髓鞘绝缘。
items.function_full_zh: 钴胺素(维生素B12)是人体内两种酶的辅酶,仅此两种。methionine synthase利用5-甲基四氢叶酸将同型半胱氨酸重新甲基化为甲硫氨酸,这一反应既能再生可用的叶酸,又能提供S-腺苷甲硫氨酸,用于维持髓鞘的甲基化反应。methylmalonyl-CoA mutase在线粒体内将甲基丙二酰辅酶A转化为琥珀酰辅酶A,参与奇数碳链脂肪酸和支链氨基酸的分解代谢。其吸收过程颇为复杂:胃酸和pepsin先将B12从食物蛋白中释放出来,壁细胞分泌的内因子负责携带它,回肠末端的受体再将其摄取。除严格素食(纯素)饮食外,缺乏的常见原因通常是这条通路上某一环节出现障碍,并非单纯摄入不足。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 恶性贫血(自身免疫性内因子缺失)及脊髓亚急性联合变性;巨幼细胞性贫血是其血液学表现。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 甲基丙二酸和同型半胱氨酸的升高早于血清B12降至明确缺乏的范围,这也是临界值结果常需进一步检测这两项代谢物的原因。手足对称性刺痛和麻木,振动觉和关节位置觉丧失,在暗处行走更不稳。可见大细胞增多伴中性粒细胞分叶过多、舌痛且舌面光滑、疲劳、轻度认知迟缓和情绪低落。即使全血细胞计数完全正常,神经系统体征也可能已经出现。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 脊髓亚急性联合变性:后索和皮质脊髓侧束脱髓鞘,导致感觉性共济失调、痉挛、跖反射呈伸性反应,以及膀胱和肠道功能紊乱,若不治疗会进展为痉挛性截瘫并丧失独立行走能力。少数患者出现视神经萎缩,也有少数患者出现痴呆和精神病性症状。可发生伴全血细胞减少的重度巨幼细胞性贫血,但真正致残的是神经系统病变。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 血液学异常可完全纠正(一周内出现网织红细胞增多,约八周内计数恢复正常),但神经系统损害未必如此。恢复在最初两个月内最快,可持续至约六个月。在已发表的最大宗病例系列中,47.1%的病例神经系统异常完全恢复,只有6.3%遗留中重度残疾;其余病例介于两者之间,残余损害的程度与治疗前缺乏的严重程度和未治疗持续的时间相关。这种血液学与神经系统恢复情况的分离,正是不明原因的大细胞性贫血不应盲目给予叶酸的原因:叶酸会纠正血象、去除这一可见信号,而脊髓损害仍在继续进展。
items.at_risk_zh: 60岁以上、患有萎缩性胃炎和食物结合型B12吸收不良的成年人。自身免疫性恶性贫血。胃切除或胃旁路手术、回肠切除、克罗恩病。长期使用二甲双胍。长期使用质子泵抑制剂或H2受体拮抗剂。严格素食者(纯素),以及重要的是,他们完全母乳喂养的婴儿。反复接触一氧化二氮(笑气),无论娱乐性使用还是职业性接触,均会直接使methionine synthase失活。
items.prevalence_zh: 在美国和英国的大型调查中,60岁及以上人群中约6%血浆B12低于148 pmol/L,另有近20%处于148至221 pmol/L的临界范围;患病率随年龄增长而上升,在低收入国家,各年龄段的患病率都明显更高(PMID 19116323)。

items.function_short_zh: 维生素B6为氨基酸代谢酶提供动力;大剂量摄入则会损伤感觉神经。
items.function_full_zh: 其活性形式磷酸吡哆醛(pyridoxal 5'-phosphate,PLP)是远超100种酶的辅酶,其中大多数参与氨基酸代谢:transaminases、合成血清素、多巴胺、γ-氨基丁酸(GABA)和组胺的decarboxylases、血红素合成的第一个限速步骤ALA synthase、glycogen phosphorylase,以及通过转硫途径清除同型半胱氨酸的cystathionine beta-synthase和cystathionine gamma-lyase。需求量随蛋白质摄入量增加而上升。一旦这些酶达到饱和,额外摄入的B6便不再增加任何功能。大剂量产品(通常为每日50至500毫克,用于经前症状、腕管综合征、孕期恶心,或隐藏在复合B族维生素和能量补充剂配方中)反而会引起剂量依赖和病程依赖的感觉神经病变,靶点为背根神经节。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血浆磷酸吡哆醛低于约20 nmol/L,通常完全没有症状。若出现症状,多为黏膜皮肤方面且无特异性:口角炎、舌炎、眼鼻口周围的脂溢性皮炎,以及易怒和情绪低落。同型半胱氨酸可能轻度升高。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 因血红素合成受损导致的低色素小细胞性贫血(有别于X连锁ALAS2型吡哆醇反应性铁粒幼细胞性贫血,这是一种遗传性疾病,不是饮食缺乏所致),以及周围感觉神经病变。婴儿缺乏时会因GABA合成障碍而出现癫痫发作。单纯性重度缺乏罕见,几乎总是继发于:异烟肼、环丝氨酸、肼屈嗪或青霉胺治疗,酒精依赖,透析,或吸收不良。需要注意的是,B6缺乏和过量都会引起周围神经病变,因此补充剂使用者出现神经病变时,由补充剂本身引起的可能性至少不低于其被补充剂纠正的可能性。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 缺乏本身在适度补充后数周内即可完全纠正。数据表中部分可逆这一分类描述的是过量情形下的恢复情况:大剂量B6引起的感觉神经病变,通常在停用补充剂后数月内改善,有时改善幅度很大,但部分人会残留麻木和位置觉障碍,因为损伤累及的是背根神经节中的感觉神经元胞体,而不仅仅是轴突。发病时间与剂量成反比,每日数克可在数周内致病,而每日数十毫克可能需要数年才会出现。
items.at_risk_zh: 缺乏方面:服用异烟肼、环丝氨酸、肼屈嗪或青霉胺的人群;酒精依赖者;透析患者;吸收不良者。老年人、吸烟者以及正在或曾经使用口服避孕药者,血浆PLP水平也较低。中毒方面:任何连续数月至数年服用大剂量B6或复合B族维生素产品的人,往往未意识到摄入剂量之高,因为单片剂量就可能数倍超过欧盟规定的可耐受最高摄入量。
items.prevalence_zh: 在2003至2004年NHANES调查中,未服用补充剂的美国成年人中约23%至27%血浆PLP低于20 nmol/L,大多只是生化指标异常而非有症状(PMID 18469270)。在毒性方面,欧洲食品安全局(EFSA)于2023年将成人可耐受最高摄入量定为每日12毫克,该数值是以每日50毫克这一引起周围神经病变的参考剂量为基础,除以不确定系数4得出的(doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006)。

items.function_short_zh: 维持胶原蛋白强度并促进伤口愈合;缺乏时血管和牙龈会发生破坏。
items.function_full_zh: 抗坏血酸(维生素C)是一类双加氧酶(dioxygenases)的还原性辅因子,负责维持其铁原子处于活性状态。其中最广为人知的是prolyl-4-hydroxylase和lysyl hydroxylase,它们使胶原蛋白发生羟化,从而使三螺旋结构保持稳定并能够交联;缺少这些反应,合成出的胶原蛋白就有缺陷,这解释了出血、伤口愈合不良以及旧疤痕重新裂开等表现。同样的化学机制也服务于dopamine beta-hydroxylase(去甲肾上腺素合成)、peptidylglycine alpha-amidating monooxygenase(肽类激素的酰胺化)、两种肉碱生物合成酶,以及基因调控中的HIF prolyl hydroxylases、TET and JmjC demethylases。抗坏血酸还能将膳食中的非血红素铁还原为可吸收的亚铁形式。由于gulonolactone oxidase基因失活,人类自身无法合成抗坏血酸。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 在摄入量低于约每日10毫克大约一至三个月后,血浆抗坏血酸水平下降,体内储存量降至约300毫克以下。第一阶段表现为疲劳、易怒和双腿弥漫性酸痛,没有任何可见体征。随后出现特征性皮肤表现:毛囊周围角化过度,大腿和小腿部位体毛呈螺旋状卷曲,毛囊周围出血,容易瘀伤;凡是尚有牙齿者,还会出现牙龈肿胀、松软、易出血。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 皮肤、肌肉和关节内出血,关节积血,以及骨膜下出血,后者在儿童中会导致严重的肢体疼痛并拒绝活动(假性瘫痪)。旧伤口和疤痕会重新裂开,牙齿松动脱落,并出现贫血和水肿。未经治疗的坏血病是致命的,通常死于出血或心力衰竭,不过在当前医疗条件下,由于治疗极易获得,病情很少会发展到这一地步。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 恢复完全,而且异常迅速。治疗开始后24至48小时内疲劳和疼痛即开始改善,牙龈出血和瘀伤在一到两周内消退,按每日100至300毫克补充,完全恢复约需三个月。不会遗留任何永久性损害。唯一的例外是已经脱落的牙齿,它们不会再长出来。
items.at_risk_zh: 饮食中几乎不含水果或蔬菜的人群:极度挑食或限制性饮食者(包括部分自闭症儿童)、独居且患有严重精神疾病或痴呆的人、酒精和药物依赖者,以及无家可归和食物无保障人群。此外还包括吸烟者(需求量约高出每日35毫克)、透析患者、吸收不良者,以及部分减重手术后患者。坏血病是一种由饮食结构导致的疾病,不是补充剂摄入不足所致;每日约10毫克即可预防,一个橙子就能轻松超过这一量。
items.prevalence_zh: 在2003至2004年NHANES调查中,美国6岁及以上人群中有7.1%(SE 0.9)血清抗坏血酸低于11.4 micromol/L,低于NHANES III调查中约13%的比例,吸烟者和低收入群体的比例最高(PMID 19675106)。

items.supplement: High-dose folic acid plus B12 for cardiovascular prevention
items.function_short_zh: 可降低血液中的同型半胱氨酸水平,但事实证明这并不能预防心脏病发作。
items.function_full_zh: 叶酸加B12,常常还加入B6,能可靠地将血浆总同型半胱氨酸水平降低约四分之一,因为这两种维生素都能促进methionine synthase这一步骤,将同型半胱氨酸转化回甲硫氨酸。这一治疗思路最初来自观察性研究:同型半胱氨酸升高与血管疾病和卒中相关。随机对照试验将这一生物标志物与疾病本身区分开来。Cochrane系统评价总共纳入15项试验、71,422名受试者;在这一总数中,降低同型半胱氨酸对心肌梗死没有影响(12项试验,46,699名受试者:7.1%对6.0%,RR 1.02,95% CI 0.95至1.10),对全因死亡也没有影响(11项试验,44,817名受试者:11.7%对12.3%,RR 1.01,95% CI 0.96至1.06),卒中方面有小幅度降低(10项试验,44,224名受试者:4.3%对5.1%,RR 0.90,95% CI 0.82至0.99),这一降低主要来自那些未实行叶酸强化、基线叶酸水平较低人群中的试验。有一个安全性问题延续自其组成成分:在未先检查B12水平的情况下给予大剂量叶酸,可能会使B12缺乏导致的贫血恢复正常,而脊髓损害却在未被察觉的情况下持续进展,因此在给予这类剂量的叶酸之前,应先明确B12状态。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。这是一种为心血管预防而测试的治疗方案,不是一种营养素。其两种组成成分各自的缺乏状态已在它们各自的条目中说明。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 不适用。复方制剂本身不存在缺乏这一说法。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。干预类别不存在缺乏状态。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。干预类别不存在缺乏状态。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用。这里给出的是效应量的数据,不是缺乏程度的数据:Cochrane的估计值为需要治疗人数(NNTB)143人(95% CI 85至428)、疗程5.4年可预防一例卒中,该数据来自在未实行叶酸强化人群中开展的叶酸加依那普利对照试验(CSPPT试验)(PMID 28816346)。

items: Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet

items.function_short: Carries oxygen in the blood and powers the enzymes that turn food into usable energy.
items.function_full: Iron sits at the centre of the haem group in haemoglobin and myoglobin, where it binds and releases oxygen, and in the iron-sulfur clusters of mitochondrial complexes I to III, where it moves electrons during ATP synthesis. It is also the cofactor for ribonucleotide reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of DNA synthesis, which is why dividing tissues (marrow, gut lining) fail first. In the developing brain it is required for tyrosine hydroxylase (dopamine synthesis), for oligodendrocyte myelination, and for hippocampal maturation, which is the mechanism behind the developmental findings in infants. Absorption is tightly regulated by hepcidin, so the body cannot simply take up more when stores are low.
items.deficiency_name: Iron deficiency anaemia (microcytic, hypochromic anaemia). Iron deficiency without anaemia is a recognised earlier stage of the same process.
items.deficiency_early: Serum ferritin falls long before haemoglobin does, so a blood test shows depleted stores while the full blood count is still normal. What a person notices at that stage: fatigue disproportionate to activity, breathlessness on stairs, cold hands, hair shedding, restless legs at night, and sometimes pica (craving ice or chalk). Ferritin is an acute-phase protein, so inflammation or infection can mask true depletion.
items.deficiency_severe: Haemoglobin falls with small pale red cells, producing pallor, tachycardia, exertional dyspnoea, and in extreme cases high-output cardiac failure. In pregnancy it raises the risk of preterm delivery, low birth weight, and poor infant iron stores. In infancy it impairs motor and cognitive development. In adults over 50 a new iron deficiency is a red flag for occult gastrointestinal bleeding and needs investigation rather than a supplement.
items.reversibility_note: In adults, anaemia and its symptoms correct fully once iron is replaced and the cause is fixed; haemoglobin typically rises within 4 to 8 weeks and stores refill over 3 to 6 months. Iron deficiency during infancy is the exception. Children with severe chronic iron deficiency in infancy still scored worse on cognitive, motor and behavioural measures more than 10 years after full iron treatment, so the developmental window matters more than the correction.
items.at_risk: Menstruating women, especially with heavy periods; pregnant women (requirement roughly doubles); infants 6 to 24 months, particularly preterm or low-birth-weight; frequent blood donors; endurance athletes; people with coeliac disease, inflammatory bowel disease, H. pylori gastritis or after bariatric surgery; vegetarian and vegan diets high in phytate; and anyone with chronic gastrointestinal blood loss.
items.prevalence: Anaemia affects about 33.7% of women aged 15 to 49 worldwide (WHO Global Health Observatory / GBD 2021), with iron deficiency the single largest cause. In the US, estimates of iron deficiency in premenopausal women range from roughly 10% to 38% depending on the ferritin cut-off used (below 15 vs below 25 micrograms/L), which is why published figures disagree so widely.
items.source: Lozoff B et al., Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2000;154:1108-1113, PMID 10742372 (persisting deficits 10 years after treatment); WHO Global Health Observatory, anaemia in women of reproductive age; Camaschella C, N Engl J Med 2015;372:1832-1843.

items.function_short: The raw material for thyroid hormone, which sets metabolic rate and builds the fetal brain.
items.function_full: Iodine has exactly one job: it is the substrate thyroid peroxidase attaches to tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin to make thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). There is no alternative pathway and no substitute element. T3 acting on nuclear thyroid hormone receptors drives basal metabolic rate and thermogenesis in adults. In the fetus it governs neuronal migration, dendritic branching, synaptogenesis and myelination, on a fixed developmental timetable. The fetal thyroid does not begin producing hormone until roughly week 12 to 16, so first-trimester brain development runs entirely on maternal T4 crossing the placenta. Maternal requirement rises to about 250 micrograms per day in pregnancy and lactation.
items.deficiency_name: Iodine deficiency disorders: endemic goitre and hypothyroidism in adults, and endemic cretinism as the severe congenital form.
items.deficiency_early: The thyroid enlarges (goitre) as TSH rises to extract more iodine from a falling supply. On testing, a population median urinary iodine concentration below 100 micrograms/L (below 150 in pregnancy) and a raised serum thyroglobulin signal inadequacy before any clinical change. A pregnant woman with mild to moderate deficiency usually notices nothing at all, which is what makes this dangerous.
items.deficiency_severe: Endemic cretinism: severe intellectual disability, deaf-mutism, spastic diplegia and stunted growth in a child whose mother was severely deficient during pregnancy. Adults develop overt hypothyroidism with cold intolerance, weight gain, bradycardia and, in extreme untreated cases, myxoedema.
