Even mild to moderate maternal deficiency is associated with lower verbal IQ and reading scores in the child, on the order of a few points, which is small individually and large across a population.
items.reversibility_note: Goitre, adult hypothyroidism and impaired thyroid function correct with iodine repletion. Brain damage sustained in utero and in the first two years of life does not. The first-trimester component of the damage is already fixed by the time a pregnancy is confirmed, so iodine given to an affected child undoes nothing; only iodine given to the mother before and during pregnancy prevents it. This is the strongest irreversibility case among common micronutrients, and the reason salt iodisation is a public health programme rather than an individual choice.
items.at_risk: Pregnant and lactating women anywhere, since requirements rise sharply. Populations in iodine-poor soil regions (mountainous and flood-plain areas) without salt iodisation. People who avoid iodised salt while also avoiding dairy, eggs and seafood, including strict vegans without a deliberate iodine source. Users of non-iodised speciality salts (pink, sea, kosher), which supply essentially no iodine.
items.prevalence: 21 countries still had insufficient population iodine intake as of 2020-2021, down from 113 in 1993, thanks to salt iodisation (IGN Global Scorecard of Iodine Nutrition). Mild to moderate deficiency in pregnant women persists in countries whose general populations are replete, including the UK, Norway and Australia. Iodine deficiency remains the leading preventable cause of intellectual disability worldwide.
items.source: Delange F et al., N Engl J Med 1994;331:1770-1771, doi:10.1056/NEJM199412293312610; Bath SC et al., Lancet 2013;382:331-337 (mild maternal deficiency and child IQ, ALSPAC); Iodine Global Network, Global Scorecard of Iodine Nutrition, ign.org/scorecard; Zimmermann MB, Lancet 2008;372:1251-1262.

items.function_short: Zinc runs hundreds of enzymes; the lozenge form targets cold symptoms in the throat.
items.function_full: Zinc is a structural or catalytic component of more than 300 enzymes and of the roughly 2,000 zinc-finger transcription factors that bind DNA, so it is required for gene expression, DNA and RNA synthesis, and cell division. Tissues with fast turnover fail first: gut mucosa, skin, growth plate cartilage, and lymphocytes. Thymic function and T-cell development are zinc-dependent, which is the basis of the immune effects. The lozenge specifically is a different proposition from nutrition: it works (where it works) by releasing ionic zinc onto the oropharyngeal mucosa, where it appears to interfere with rhinovirus replication and ICAM-1 binding locally. That is a short-course pharmacological use in someone whose zinc status is usually normal. Lozenges are a poor way to correct systemic deficiency, and sustained high-dose zinc (above roughly 40 mg/day) induces intestinal metallothionein and causes copper deficiency with anaemia and myelopathy.
items.deficiency_name: Nutritional zinc deficiency (growth failure, chronic diarrhoea, impaired immunity, characteristic dermatitis). Acrodermatitis enteropathica is the inherited form, caused by SLC39A4 mutations impairing zinc uptake, and is a genetic disorder rather than a consequence of diet.
items.deficiency_early: Blunted taste and smell, poor appetite, slow wound healing, and infections that are more frequent and last longer. In children, growth velocity crosses centiles downward before any skin change appears. There is no good early biomarker: plasma zinc falls only late, drops during any inflammatory episode, and varies with time of day and recent meals, so a normal plasma zinc does not exclude deficiency.
items.deficiency_severe: Stunting and delayed sexual maturation in children, persistent diarrhoea that worsens the deficiency in a loop, alopecia, and a distinctive bullous, crusted dermatitis around the mouth, eyes, genitals and on the hands and feet. Cell-mediated immunity is impaired, with thymic atrophy and reduced T-cell counts. In young children in low-income settings, zinc deficiency contributes measurably to deaths from diarrhoeal disease and pneumonia.
items.reversibility_note: Dermatitis, taste disturbance, diarrhoea and immune function recover within days to a few weeks of repletion, and the response is often dramatic. Linear growth is the part that does not fully catch up: height lost during a prolonged deficiency spanning a growth period is only partly recovered, and final adult stature can remain reduced.
items.at_risk: People on cereal-based diets high in phytate with little animal protein, which is the dominant global pattern. Children in low-income settings. Malabsorption from Crohn's disease, coeliac disease or short bowel; bariatric surgery. Chronic alcohol use, which causes urinary zinc loss. Chronic diarrhoea, sickle cell disease, and older adults with restricted intake. High-dose supplemental iron taken at the same time competes for the same absorptive route.
items.prevalence: An estimated 17.3% of the world's population is at risk of inadequate zinc intake, based on national food-supply zinc availability (Wessells and Brown, 2012). Clinically overt nutritional zinc deficiency in healthy adults in high-income countries is uncommon.
items.source: Wessells KR, Brown KH. PLoS One 2012;7:e50568, PMID 23209782; King JC et al., J Nutr 2016;146:858S-885S (IZiNCG biomarkers); Hemila H, BMJ Open 2017;7:e013295 (zinc lozenges and cold duration); NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, Zinc Fact Sheet for Health Professionals.

items.function_short: Selenium builds the enzymes that mop up oxidative damage and switch on thyroid hormone.
items.function_full: Selenium is incorporated as the amino acid selenocysteine into about 25 human selenoproteins. The glutathione peroxidases (GPX1 to GPX4) reduce hydrogen peroxide and lipid hydroperoxides, GPX4 specifically preventing ferroptotic membrane damage. Thioredoxin reductases maintain cellular redox state and support DNA synthesis. The iodothyronine deiodinases convert T4 to active T3, which links selenium status to thyroid function. Selenoprotein P is the plasma transport form and the best status marker. The dose in this entry matters: plasma glutathione peroxidase and selenoprotein P saturate at intakes of roughly 55 to 75 micrograms per day, so 200 micrograms per day supplies three to four times the adult RDA and produces no further enzyme activity in someone already replete, while sitting halfway to the tolerable upper limit of 400 micrograms per day. In the Nutritional Prevention of Cancer trial, 200 micrograms per day for a mean 7.7 years raised type 2 diabetes incidence (hazard ratio 1.55, 95% CI 1.03 to 2.33), concentrated in participants who started in the highest baseline selenium tertile (hazard ratio 2.70).
items.deficiency_name: Keshan disease, an endemic cardiomyopathy. Kashin-Beck disease, an endemic osteoarthropathy, occurs in the same low-selenium regions and is associated with, though not fully explained by, selenium deficiency.
items.deficiency_early: Plasma selenium and glutathione peroxidase activity fall with no symptoms at all. In endemic areas, subclinical ECG abnormalities and reduced ejection fraction appear before overt illness, which is how latent Keshan disease is detected on screening. Isolated cases outside endemic areas typically surface as unexplained myopathy, muscle pain, or whitened nail beds.
items.deficiency_severe: Keshan disease presents acutely with cardiogenic shock and arrhythmia, or chronically as congestive cardiomyopathy with cardiac enlargement and multifocal myocardial necrosis and fibrosis. It classically strikes children and women of childbearing age in low-soil-selenium areas and is fatal without treatment. A coxsackievirus co-factor is thought to trigger the acute form in a selenium-depleted host. Kashin-Beck disease destroys growth-plate and articular cartilage, producing shortened fingers, deformed ankles, knees, wrists and elbows, and permanently limited movement.
items.reversibility_note: Early Keshan disease responds well to selenium replacement, and heart failure can improve substantially or resolve if caught before the myocardium is remodelled. Once dilated cardiomyopathy with established fibrosis has developed, the myocardial damage does not fully reverse and outcomes are poor. Kashin-Beck cartilage necrosis and the resulting joint deformity are permanent. Prophylactic sodium selenite in endemic Chinese counties prevented new cases, which is the clearest evidence the causal direction is right.
items.at_risk: Residents of low-selenium soil belts, chiefly the diagonal band across China from the northeast to the southwest, plus parts of Siberia. Long-term parenteral nutrition without added selenium. Severe malabsorption, short bowel, and cystic fibrosis. Dialysis patients. Dietary selenium deficiency is not a realistic concern for anyone eating a mixed diet in North America, where soil selenium is high; two Brazil nuts alone exceed the adult RDA.
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED as a current global figure. Keshan disease was endemic across a defined low-selenium region of China and has been reduced to near-zero incidence since selenite supplementation and food-supply changes began in the 1970s. Dietary selenium deficiency is essentially absent in the United States, where median intake already exceeds the RDA from food alone.
items.source: Stranges S et al., Ann Intern Med 2007;147:217-223, PMID 17620655 (200 µg/d and type 2 diabetes, NPC trial); Rayman MP, Lancet 2012;379:1256-1268; Keshan Disease, StatPearls, NCBI Bookshelf NBK603722; Institute of Medicine DRI for selenium (RDA 55 µg/d, UL 400 µg/d).

items.function_short: A cofactor in hundreds of reactions; every molecule of ATP works bound to magnesium.
items.function_full: The biologically active form of ATP is Mg-ATP, so magnesium is an obligate participant in every kinase reaction, every ATPase and both DNA and RNA polymerases, more than 300 enzymes in total. It acts as a physiological calcium antagonist: it blocks the NMDA receptor channel at rest and dampens calcium entry in vascular smooth muscle and myocardium, which is why depletion raises neuromuscular excitability and arrhythmia risk. Magnesium is also required both for parathyroid hormone secretion and for end-organ response to it, so depletion produces a hypocalcaemia that will not correct until magnesium is replaced. About 60% of body magnesium is locked in bone and most of the rest is intracellular, leaving only about 1% in serum. Serum magnesium is therefore a poor guide to total body status and can be normal in a genuinely depleted person.
items.deficiency_name: Symptomatic hypomagnesaemia (ICD-10 E83.4). There is no eponymous deficiency disease; the severe presentation is hypomagnesaemic tetany with refractory hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia. Inherited renal magnesium wasting (Gitelman syndrome, familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria) is a genetic tubular disorder rather than a dietary deficiency.
items.deficiency_early: Usually nothing at all. Low dietary intake shows up as intake below the estimated average requirement with a normal serum magnesium, because the kidney conserves aggressively. The first things a person notices are muscle cramps, eyelid or hand tremor, and irritability or poor sleep, all of which are non-specific. In practice a low serum magnesium is most often spotted incidentally on a metabolic panel run for unexplained hypokalaemia or hypocalcaemia.
items.deficiency_severe: Tetany with positive Chvostek and Trousseau signs, paraesthesiae, seizures, and cardiac arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation and torsades de pointes. Accompanying hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia resist correction until magnesium itself is replaced, which is the clinically important teaching point. Severe cases are almost always driven by drug or gastrointestinal or renal losses rather than by diet alone.
items.reversibility_note: Repletion corrects the neuromuscular and cardiac features and allows the linked potassium and calcium abnormalities to correct, with no residual deficit once the underlying cause is addressed. The one caveat is timing rather than permanence: serum magnesium normalises before body stores do, so bone and intracellular pools take days to weeks to refill and stopping too early lets the deficit return.
items.at_risk: Chronic alcohol use (the single most common cause). Chronic diarrhoea, malabsorption, short bowel and after bariatric surgery. Long-term proton pump inhibitor use, which can cause profound hypomagnesaemia. Loop and thiazide diuretics, cisplatin, amphotericin, and calcineurin inhibitors. Poorly controlled diabetes with osmotic diuresis. Refeeding syndrome. In someone with normal kidneys and a normal gut, diet alone rarely produces symptomatic deficiency.
items.prevalence: About 48% of Americans of all ages consume less magnesium from food and beverages than their estimated average requirement (NHANES 2013-2016). Clinically significant hypomagnesaemia is far less common than that figure suggests: roughly 2% in the general population, rising to about 10% to 20% of hospitalised patients and higher in intensive care. The gap between the two numbers is the reason low intake is often overstated as widespread deficiency.
items.source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, Magnesium Health Professional Fact Sheet, ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Magnesium-HealthProfessional (NHANES 2013-2016 intake data); Ayuk J, Gittoes NJL, Ann Clin Biochem 2014;51:179-188 (contemporary view of hypomagnesaemia); Gragossian A et al., Hypomagnesemia, StatPearls, NCBI Bookshelf NBK500003.

items.supplement: Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet
items.function_short: Builds bone mineral and carries the signals for muscle contraction, nerve firing and clotting.
items.function_full: About 99% of body calcium is hydroxyapatite crystal in bone and teeth, serving a structural role. The remaining 1% is the cell's universal second messenger: it triggers excitation-contraction coupling in muscle, neurotransmitter release at synapses, and several steps of the coagulation cascade. Serum ionised calcium is defended within a very narrow range by parathyroid hormone, calcitriol and bone resorption, so a low dietary intake does not lower blood calcium. It is paid for out of the skeleton instead. That regulation is the key to this particular entry. Fractional absorption falls as intake rises, so in a person already meeting requirements from food, additional supplemental calcium contributes little to bone mineral and the surplus is largely excreted. What a supplement does add that food does not is a large absorptive bolus, and that is the context for the constipation, the increased kidney stone risk seen in the Women's Health Initiative, and the contested cardiovascular signal.
items.deficiency_name: Calcium-deficiency rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults, with nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism. This is a disease of genuinely low intake and has no bearing on whether someone eating an adequate diet adds a supplement.
items.deficiency_early: Nothing a person notices. Biochemically, parathyroid hormone rises while serum calcium stays normal, urinary calcium falls, and bone turnover markers climb. The skeleton is being drawn on silently, which is why the early phase is only ever detected on testing done for another reason.
items.deficiency_severe: In children, rickets with bowed legs, widened wrists and costochondral junctions, bone pain and delayed growth. In adults, osteomalacia with diffuse bone pain, proximal muscle weakness and pseudofractures, and over decades accelerated bone loss with increased fragility fracture risk. Symptomatic hypocalcaemia with tetany and paraesthesiae comes from parathyroid or vitamin D failure rather than from dietary shortfall alone, because the skeleton buffers intake so effectively.
items.reversibility_note: Rickets and osteomalacia heal with calcium repletion (plus vitamin D where that is also deficient), and bone mineral density largely restores. Two things do not fully recover: skeletal deformity already established in a growing child, along with the height lost to it, and peak bone mass never accrued during adolescence, which sets the lifetime baseline and cannot be rebuilt later by supplementing.
items.at_risk: Children on low-calcium, high-phytate diets in parts of sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, where dietary intakes around 200 mg/day have been documented. Adults with no dairy and no fortified alternatives. Malabsorption, post-gastrectomy states, long-term corticosteroid use, and untreated coeliac disease. The population this entry describes, someone whose diet already meets requirements, is not at risk by definition, which is the whole point.
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED as a global figure for calcium-specific deficiency, because it is difficult to separate from vitamin D deficiency in survey data. Regionally it is well documented: mean dietary calcium intake in Nigerian children with nutritional rickets was 217 mg/day against a requirement of roughly 700 to 1,300 mg/day depending on age, and calcium alone outperformed vitamin D alone in treating them.
items.source: Thacher TD et al., N Engl J Med 1999;341:563-568, PMID 10451461 (calcium vs vitamin D for nutritional rickets); Institute of Medicine, Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D, 2011, doi:10.17226/13050; Jackson RD et al., N Engl J Med 2006;354:669-683 (WHI: calcium plus vitamin D, fracture and renal stone outcomes).

items.function_short: Not a nutrient. Gut and mouth bacteria turn it into nitric oxide, which widens blood vessels.
items.function_full: Inorganic nitrate from beetroot and leafy greens is absorbed in the proximal small intestine, and roughly a quarter of the circulating pool is actively concentrated by the salivary glands. Commensal bacteria on the posterior tongue reduce it to nitrite, and swallowed nitrite is further reduced to nitric oxide in the acidic stomach and in hypoxic tissue by deoxyhaemoglobin, deoxymyoglobin, xanthine oxidoreductase and other metalloproteins. This enterosalivary route is a supplementary supply line that runs in parallel with the body's own synthesis of nitric oxide from L-arginine by nitric oxide synthase, which is the primary and always-available pathway. That distinction is what makes nitrate a usable substrate rather than a required nutrient: NOS-derived nitric oxide continues normally on a nitrate-free diet. Measured effects are pharmacological and dose-dependent: vasodilation with a modest fall in blood pressure, and a reduced oxygen cost of submaximal exercise. Antibacterial mouthwash abolishes the effect entirely by killing the nitrate-reducing oral flora, which is the clearest demonstration that the mechanism is microbial rather than nutritional.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. No one becomes deficient in dietary nitrate, because the body has no requirement for it and synthesises nitric oxide independently. A person eating no beetroot and no leafy greens has lower plasma nitrite and forgoes the blood pressure and exercise-economy effects, which is a missed pharmacological benefit rather than a deficiency state.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE. Dietary nitrate is not an essential nutrient and has no deficiency state, so no prevalence figure exists and none should be quoted. For scale of the effect rather than of a deficiency, pooled trials report systolic blood pressure reductions of roughly 3 to 5 mmHg, largest in hypertensive participants.
items.source: Lundberg JO, Weitzberg E, Gladwin MT. Nat Rev Drug Discov 2008;7:156-167, doi:10.1038/nrd2466 (nitrate-nitrite-nitric oxide pathway); Jackson JK et al., J Nutr 2018;148:1749-1762 (inorganic nitrate and beetroot juice, blood pressure meta-analysis); Govoni M et al., Nitric Oxide 2008;19:333-337 (antibacterial mouthwash abolishes the effect).

errors.correction: The hepcidin sentence inverts the physiology. In iron deficiency hepcidin is suppressed, ferroportin survives on enterocytes and macrophages, and fractional absorption rises several-fold (roughly 10% to 20-30% of intake). The body does take up more when stores are low. The two true statements are that there is no regulated excretion route, and that absorption is capped in rate so a large deficit still takes months to refill, and that in inflammation hepcidin stays high so uptake fails despite empty stores. Rewrite as: hepcidin caps how fast stores can be refilled and blocks absorption during inflammation, which is why oral iron works slowly and why inflammatory anaemia does not respond to it.
errors.source: Camaschella C, N Engl J Med 2015;372:1832-1843 (the entry's own cited review); Ganz T, Nemeth E, hepcidin/ferroportin axis

errors.correction: PMID 10742372 is Lozoff B, Jimenez E, Hagen J, Mollen E, Wolf AW, 'Poorer behavioral and developmental outcome more than 10 years after treatment for iron deficiency in infancy', Pediatrics 2000;105(4):e51. It is not Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2000;154:1108-1113. The PMID and the journal locator in this entry point at different things. Replace the journal, volume and page fields with the Pediatrics citation.
errors.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10742372/ and publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article-abstract/105/4/e51

errors.correction: 33.7% is not a WHO Global Health Observatory figure. WHO's 2019 estimates give about 30% for non-pregnant and 36-37% for pregnant women aged 15-49, roughly 29.9% overall. The 33.7% comes from GBD 2021, where the age-standardised prevalence rate for women of reproductive age is 33,716.77 per 100,000. Attribute the number to GBD 2021 alone, or quote WHO's ~30% if WHO is the intended source.
errors.source: WHO anaemia fact sheet and GHO indicator (30% non-pregnant, 37% pregnant, 2019); GBD 2021 anemia analysis, PMC12338041 (33,716.77 per 100,000)

errors.correction: The 10% to 38% range for US premenopausal women mixes two different populations. The 38-39% figure at ferritin below 25 is from Weyand et al., JAMA 2023, in females aged 12 to 21 years. In a 62,685-woman US and Canadian sample (mean age 49.6) ferritin below 15 gave 7.43% and ferritin below 25 gave 15.33%; restricted to ages 25-54 the three definitions spanned 4.46% to 21.23%. State the age band each end of the range comes from, or narrow the claim to adolescents and young women.
errors.source: Weyand AC et al., JAMA 2023;329(24):2191-2193; 'Prevalence of Iron Deficiency Using 3 Definitions Among Women in the US and Canada', PMID 38848068

errors.correction: 'The first-trimester component of the damage is already fixed by the time a pregnancy is confirmed' is contradicted by the trial the entry's own source set accompanies. Cao et al. found that iodine given in the first or second trimester left only 2% of infants with moderate or severe neurologic abnormality versus 9% when given in the third trimester or after birth, and concluded that treatment up to the end of the second trimester protects the fetal brain. The window closes around the end of the second trimester, not at pregnancy confirmation. This matters practically: it turns 'too late, do not bother' into 'start immediately'. The IRREVERSIBLE classification itself is correct and should stand.
errors.source: Cao XY et al., N Engl J Med 1994;331:1739-1744, PMID 7984194

errors.correction: N Engl J Med 1994;331:1770-1771, doi:10.1056/NEJM199412293312610, is an editorial by B. S. Hetzel titled 'Iodine deficiency and fetal brain damage' (PMID 7984200), not a Delange paper. Either re-attribute to Hetzel BS or, better, cite the primary trial it comments on: Cao XY et al., N Engl J Med 1994;331:1739-1744, doi:10.1056/NEJM199412293312603.
errors.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7984200/

errors.correction: BMJ Open 2017;7:e013295 (doi 10.1136/bmjopen-2016-013295) is Mohn J et al., a pilot study of a group intervention for diabetes-related emotional distress in type 1 diabetes. It has nothing to do with zinc or colds. Hemila's zinc lozenge evidence is Hemila H et al., Br J Clin Pharmacol 2016;82:1393-1398 (individual patient data meta-analysis, zinc acetate lozenges) and Hemila H, JRSM Open 2017;8(5):2054270417694291 (zinc acetate vs gluconate and dose).
errors.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38852025/ and PMC5061795 (Br J Clin Pharmacol 2016 IPD meta-analysis)

errors.correction: 'Above roughly 40 mg/day ... causes copper deficiency with anaemia and myelopathy' overstates the threshold. 40 mg/day is the tolerable upper intake level, derived from a marginal fall in erythrocyte superoxide dismutase at around 60 mg/day, which is a biochemical rather than a clinical endpoint. Frank copper-deficiency anaemia and myeloneuropathy are reported with sustained intakes in the region of 100-300 mg/day, typically from high-dose supplements or zinc-containing denture cream. Reword to: sustained intake above the 40 mg/day upper limit progressively impairs copper status, and prolonged intake several times higher than that can produce copper-deficiency anaemia and myeloneuropathy.
errors.source: NIH ODS Zinc Fact Sheet for Health Professionals (UL 40 mg/d, basis and copper interaction); published zinc-induced copper deficiency myeloneuropathy case series

errors.correction: 'Plasma glutathione peroxidase and selenoprotein P saturate at roughly 55 to 75 micrograms per day' collapses two different plateaus and one unresolved literature. Plasma GPX3 plateaus near 55 micrograms per day, which is what the RDA is built on. Selenoprotein P plateau estimates diverge by baseline status: about 49 micrograms per day in selenium-deficient Chinese subjects, versus about 105 micrograms per day total intake in UK adults (a 50 microgram supplement on top of roughly 55 micrograms habitual). Quote roughly 50 to 105 micrograms per day depending on baseline status. The argument that 200 micrograms per day adds no enzyme activity in a replete person is unaffected.
errors.source: Hurst R et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2010, 'Establishing optimal selenium status', PMID 20181815; Xia Y et al., selenoprotein P optimisation in selenium-deficient Chinese subjects, PMC2921536

errors.correction: 'Roughly 2% in the general population' is below what the cited source says. Ayuk and Gittoes, Ann Clin Biochem 2014, put the general-population prevalence of hypomagnesaemia at 2.5% to 15%. Quote 2.5% to 15%. The entry's rhetorical point, that low intake is not the same as clinical deficiency, survives the correction, though the gap it describes narrows.
errors.source: Ayuk J, Gittoes NJL, Ann Clin Biochem 2014;51:179-188, PMID 24402002 (2.5-15% general population)

errors.correction: 'Chronic alcohol use (the single most common cause)' is a ranking claim that none of the cited sources supports. Alcohol use disorder is one of the common causes, but gastrointestinal and renal losses, loop and thiazide diuretics, and proton pump inhibitors account for a large share of clinically encountered hypomagnesaemia, and drug causes dominate in hospital populations. Drop 'the single most common' and list alcohol among the leading causes.
errors.source: Ayuk J, Gittoes NJL, Ann Clin Biochem 2014;51:179-188; Gragossian A et al., Hypomagnesemia, StatPearls NBK500003

errors.supplement: Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet
errors.correction: The cited trial does not report 217 mg/day, and does not report a mean. Thacher et al. give a MEDIAN daily dietary calcium intake of 203 mg in the Nigerian children with rickets and 196 mg in controls (P=0.64). Change to 'median dietary calcium intake of about 203 mg/day'. The accompanying claim that calcium outperformed vitamin D is correct: 61% (calcium) and 58% (combination) versus 19% (vitamin D alone) reached the combined endpoint.
errors.source: Thacher TD et al., N Engl J Med 1999;341:563-568, PMID 10451461

errors.correction: 'Jackson JK et al., J Nutr 2018;148:1749-1762' does not resolve. The Jackson JK meta-analysis is 'The role of inorganic nitrate and nitrite in cardiovascular disease risk factors: a systematic review and meta-analysis of human evidence', Nutr Rev 2018;76(5):348-371, doi 10.1093/nutrit/nuy005, PMID 29506204. If the intent was specifically the beetroot blood pressure pooled estimate behind the 3 to 5 mmHg figure, cite Siervo M et al., J Nutr 2013;143:818-826 (systolic reduction of 4.4 mmHg). The 3 to 5 mmHg number itself is well supported; only the locator is wrong.
errors.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29506204/ (Nutr Rev 2018;76:348-371); Siervo M et al., J Nutr 2013;143:818-826, PMID 23596162

chk.coverage: CLEAN. All seven assigned names present exactly once: Iron, Iodine, Zinc lozenges, Selenium at 200 µg/d, Magnesium, Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet, Dietary nitrate / beetroot. No duplicates, no unassigned extras.
chk.net: The classification layer holds up; the sourcing layer does not. Priority 1 is clean: every item here is an essential mineral except dietary nitrate, which is correctly NONE / NA, and its at_risk and prevalence fields explicitly refuse to manufacture a deficiency. Priority 2 is clean: iodine is IRREVERSIBLE as required, magnesium FULL is right, and the three PARTIAL calls (iron, zinc, selenium, calcium) each name a specific non-recovering component that the literature supports (Lozoff's persisting deficits at 10-14 years; incomplete catch-up in linear growth; established Keshan fibrosis and permanent Kashin-Beck cartilage destruction; unaccrued peak bone mass). Priority 3 is clean and unusually well handled: the zinc entry names acrodermatitis enteropathica as SLC39A4-mediated and genetic, and the magnesium entry does the same for Gitelman and familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria, in both cases inside the deficiency_name field where a reader would otherwise conflate them. The failures are concentrated in priorities 4 and 5. Four of seven entries carry a citation that points at the wrong paper or at a locator that does not exist: the iron PMID and journal name disagree, the iodine editorial is Hetzel not Delange, the zinc lozenge citation is a type 1 diabetes distress pilot study, and the nitrate citation gives a Journal of Nutrition volume and page that do not resolve to the Jackson meta-analysis. Verified as correct and left alone: the selenium NPC numbers (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.03-2.33, mean 7.7 years, highest-tertile HR 2.70), the zinc 17.3% from Wessells and Brown, the magnesium 48% NHANES 2013-2016 figure, the IGN 21-countries-down-from-113 scorecard, and the Thacher finding that calcium beat vitamin D. Two substantive content errors matter more than the citation hygiene. The iron entry inverts hepcidin physiology, telling the reader the body cannot increase uptake when stores are low, when the opposite is true and the real constraints are rate and inflammation. The iodine reversibility note claims the first-trimester damage is already fixed once a pregnancy is confirmed, which the companion trial to its own cited editorial contradicts: iodine given up to the end of the second trimester still protected the fetal brain. That one is the most actionable error in the group, because it converts a reason to start supplementing immediately into a reason not to bother.

items.function_short_zh: 在血液中运送氧气,并驱动将食物转化为可用能量的酶系统。
items.function_full_zh: 铁位于血红蛋白和肌红蛋白血红素基团的中心,负责结合和释放氧气;也存在于线粒体复合物I至III的铁硫簇中,在ATP合成过程中传递电子。铁还是DNA合成限速酶ribonucleotide reductase(核糖核苷酸还原酶)的辅因子,这也是快速分裂组织(骨髓、肠道黏膜)最先受影响的原因。在发育中的大脑里,铁是tyrosine hydroxylase(酪氨酸羟化酶,多巴胺合成所需)、少突胶质细胞髓鞘形成以及海马成熟所必需的,这正是婴儿期发育相关发现背后的机制。铁调素(hepcidin)限制了储存铁被重新填满的速度,并在炎症期间阻断吸收,这就是口服铁剂起效缓慢、炎症性贫血对铁剂治疗无反应的原因。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 缺铁性贫血(小细胞低色素性贫血)。无贫血的缺铁是同一病理过程中公认的更早期阶段。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血清铁蛋白下降的时间远早于血红蛋白,因此血液检查会显示储存铁已耗竭,而全血细胞计数仍然正常。在这一阶段,人们会注意到:与活动量不成比例的疲劳、爬楼梯气短、手脚发凉、脱发、夜间不宁腿,有时还有异食癖(渴望咀嚼冰块或粉笔)。铁蛋白是一种急性期蛋白,因此炎症或感染可能掩盖真实的铁缺乏程度。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 血红蛋白下降,红细胞变小变淡,导致面色苍白、心动过速、活动后呼吸困难,极端情况下可出现高输出量心力衰竭。在孕期,缺铁会增加早产、低出生体重以及婴儿铁储备不足的风险。在婴儿期,缺铁会损害运动和认知发育。对50岁以上成人而言,新发缺铁是隐匿性消化道出血的警示信号,需要进行检查,而不是单纯补充铁剂。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 在成人中,一旦补充铁剂并纠正病因,贫血及其症状可完全恢复;血红蛋白通常在4到8周内回升,储存铁则在3到6个月内补足。婴儿期缺铁是例外。婴儿期曾患严重慢性缺铁的儿童,在接受充分铁剂治疗10多年后,认知、运动和行为测评得分依然较差,说明发育窗口期比事后纠正更为关键。
items.at_risk_zh: 有月经的女性,尤其是月经量大者;孕妇(需求量大约翻倍);6到24个月的婴幼儿,尤其是早产儿或低出生体重儿;经常献血者;耐力运动员;患有乳糜泻、炎症性肠病、H. pylori胃炎或做过减重手术的人群;植酸含量高的素食和纯素饮食者;以及任何有慢性消化道失血的人。
items.prevalence_zh: 全球15至49岁女性中约33.7%患有贫血(GBD 2021数据),其中缺铁是最主要的单一病因。世界卫生组织2019年的估计数值更低,同龄段非孕妇女约30%,孕妇约36%至37%。在美国,女性缺铁患病率因年龄段和所采用的铁蛋白临界值而差异很大:12至21岁女性以铁蛋白低于25微克/升为标准时约为38%至39%;而在一项平均年龄49.6岁的美国及加拿大女性样本中,铁蛋白低于15微克/升时为7.4%,低于25微克/升时为15.3%;若限定在25至54岁年龄段,三种不同定义下的患病率介于约4.5%至21.2%之间。

items.function_short_zh: 甲状腺激素的原料,决定代谢率并构建胎儿大脑。
items.function_full_zh: 碘只有一项功能:它是thyroid peroxidase(甲状腺过氧化物酶)用来将碘连接到甲状腺球蛋白酪氨酸残基上、合成甲状腺素(T4)和三碘甲状腺原氨酸(T3)的底物。没有替代途径,也没有其他元素可以取代碘。T3作用于细胞核内的甲状腺激素受体,决定成人的基础代谢率和产热。在胎儿体内,碘按照固定的发育时间表控制神经元迁移、树突分支、突触形成和髓鞘形成。胎儿甲状腺大约要到第12至16周才开始分泌激素,因此孕早期的大脑发育完全依赖经胎盘传递的母体T4。孕期和哺乳期母体的碘需求量上升至每日约250微克。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 碘缺乏病:成人表现为地方性甲状腺肿和甲状腺功能减退,重度先天性形式为地方性克汀病。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 随着促甲状腺激素(TSH)升高以从减少的碘供应中提取更多碘,甲状腺会增大,形成甲状腺肿。在检测中,人群尿碘中位浓度低于100微克/升(孕期低于150微克/升)以及血清甲状腺球蛋白升高,会在任何临床变化出现之前就提示碘摄入不足。轻中度缺碘的孕妇通常完全没有察觉,这正是危险所在。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 地方性克汀病:母亲孕期严重缺碘的儿童会出现重度智力障碍、聋哑、痉挛性双侧瘫痪和生长发育迟滞。成人则出现明显的甲状腺功能减退,表现为怕冷、体重增加、心动过缓,极端未治疗病例可发展为黏液性水肿。即使是轻中度的母体缺碘,也与儿童较低的语言智商和阅读成绩相关,幅度只有几分,个体层面看似不大,但放到人群层面影响很大。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 甲状腺肿、成人甲状腺功能减退和甲状腺功能受损,在补碘后可以恢复。但在子宫内及出生后头两年内造成的脑损伤则无法恢复。碘在孕早期或孕中期补充,仍能保护胎儿大脑:一项对照试验显示,在孕早期或孕中期给予治疗,只有2%的婴儿出现中重度神经系统异常,而在孕晚期或出生后才给予治疗的比例为9%。因此这一窗口期是在孕中期结束前关闭,而不是在确认怀孕时就已关闭;真正能预防损伤的是孕期给母亲补碘,而不是孩子出生后再补。这仍是常见微量营养素中不可逆性表现最强的一个例子,也是食盐加碘作为公共卫生项目而非个人选择的原因。
items.at_risk_zh: 无论身处何地,孕期和哺乳期女性都因需求量急剧上升而处于风险中。土壤缺碘地区(山区和洪泛平原地区)若未实行食盐加碘,当地人群也面临风险。既不吃加碘盐、又不吃乳制品、鸡蛋和海鲜的人,包括未刻意补充碘来源的严格素食者。使用非加碘特色盐(玫瑰盐、海盐、犹太盐)的人,这类盐基本不含碘。
items.prevalence_zh: 得益于食盐加碘,截至2020至2021年,全球仍有21个国家人群碘摄入不足,较1993年的113个大幅下降(IGN全球碘营养记分卡)。在英国、挪威和澳大利亚等一般人群碘摄入已充足的国家,孕妇中轻中度缺碘依然存在。碘缺乏仍是全球可预防性智力障碍的首要病因。

items.function_short_zh: 锌驱动数百种酶的运作;含片剂型则针对咽喉部位的感冒症状。
items.function_full_zh: 锌是300多种酶的结构或催化组分,也是约2000种与DNA结合的zinc-finger transcription factors(锌指转录因子)的组分,因此是基因表达、DNA和RNA合成以及细胞分裂所必需的。更新速度快的组织最先受影响:肠道黏膜、皮肤、生长板软骨和淋巴细胞。胸腺功能和T细胞发育都依赖锌,这是其免疫作用的基础。含片这种剂型与营养补充完全是两回事:它(在起效时)通过向口咽黏膜释放离子锌发挥作用,似乎能在局部干扰rhinovirus(鼻病毒)复制及其与ICAM-1的结合。这是一种短程药理学用途,使用者的锌营养状态通常本就正常。含片并不是纠正全身性缺锌的有效手段;长期摄入超过每日40毫克的上限会逐渐损害铜的营养状态,而持续摄入达到该上限数倍以上的剂量,则可能导致铜缺乏性贫血和脊髓神经病变。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 营养性缺锌(生长发育不良、慢性腹泻、免疫功能受损、特征性皮炎)。acrodermatitis enteropathica(肠病性肢端皮炎)是遗传型,由SLC39A4基因突变导致锌吸收障碍引起,属于遗传性疾病,而非饮食所致。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 味觉和嗅觉迟钝、食欲不振、伤口愈合缓慢,感染更频繁且病程更长。在儿童中,生长速度会先跨越百分位曲线向下偏移,之后才出现皮肤改变。目前没有理想的早期生物标志物:血浆锌只在缺乏较晚期才下降,任何炎症发作都会使其降低,且其水平还随一天中的时间和近期进食而波动,因此血浆锌正常并不能排除缺锌。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 儿童出现生长迟缓和性成熟延迟,持续性腹泻又反过来加重缺锌形成恶性循环,还有脱发,以及口周、眼周、生殖器和手足部位特征性的大疱性结痂皮炎。细胞免疫功能受损,表现为胸腺萎缩和T细胞计数下降。在低收入地区的幼儿中,缺锌对腹泻和肺炎导致的死亡有可测量的促进作用。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 补锌后,皮炎、味觉障碍、腹泻和免疫功能会在数天到数周内恢复,且改善往往十分显著。身高增长是无法完全追赶回来的部分:如果长期缺锌横跨了一段生长期,损失的身高只能部分恢复,成年后的最终身高可能仍然偏矮。
items.at_risk_zh: 以谷物为主、植酸含量高而动物蛋白摄入少的饮食人群,这是全球最普遍的膳食模式。低收入地区的儿童。因克罗恩病、乳糜泻或短肠综合征导致吸收不良的人群,以及做过减重手术者。长期饮酒者,因为酒精会导致尿锌流失增加。慢性腹泻患者、镰状细胞病患者,以及摄入受限的老年人。同时服用大剂量铁补充剂会与锌竞争同一吸收途径。
items.prevalence_zh: 根据各国食物供应中锌可利用量估算,全球约17.3%的人口存在锌摄入不足的风险(Wessells and Brown, 2012)。在高收入国家健康成年人中,临床上明显的营养性缺锌并不常见。

items.function_short_zh: 硒构成清除氧化损伤和激活甲状腺激素的各种酶。
items.function_full_zh: 硒以硒代半胱氨酸(selenocysteine)的形式,掺入人体约25种硒蛋白中。glutathione peroxidases(谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶,GPX1至GPX4)可还原过氧化氢和脂质氢过氧化物,其中GPX4尤其能防止铁死亡导致的膜损伤。thioredoxin reductases(硫氧还蛋白还原酶)维持细胞氧化还原状态并支持DNA合成。iodothyronine deiodinases(碘甲状腺原氨酸脱碘酶)将T4转化为具有活性的T3,这就是硒状态与甲状腺功能相关联的原因。selenoprotein P(硒蛋白P)是血浆中的转运形式,也是评估硒营养状态的最佳指标。本条目中的剂量很关键:血浆谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶(GPX3)在每日摄入约55微克时达到饱和,而硒蛋白P的饱和点因基线状态不同而有差异,在硒缺乏人群中约为每日49微克,在硒营养已充足的英国成人中总摄入量约需105微克,因此饱和范围大致在每日50至105微克之间,具体取决于基线状态。因此,每日200微克相当于成人推荐膳食摄入量(RDA)的三到四倍,对于硒状态已经充足的人不会带来额外的酶活性提升,同时也已达到每日400微克可耐受最高摄入量的一半。在Nutritional Prevention of Cancer试验(营养预防癌症试验)中,每日200微克、平均服用7.7年,使2型糖尿病发病率上升(风险比1.55,95%置信区间1.03至2.33),这一效应主要集中在基线硒水平处于最高三分位的参与者中(风险比2.70)。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 克山病(Keshan disease),一种地方性心肌病。大骨节病(Kashin-Beck disease)是一种地方性骨关节病,发生在同样的低硒地区,与硒缺乏有关,但硒缺乏并不能完全解释其病因。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血浆硒水平和谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶活性下降,但完全没有症状。在流行地区,亚临床心电图异常和射血分数下降会先于明显疾病出现,这也是筛查中发现潜伏型克山病的方法。流行地区之外的散发病例,通常表现为原因不明的肌病、肌肉疼痛或指甲床变白。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 克山病的急性型表现为心源性休克和心律失常,慢性型则表现为充血性心肌病,伴心脏增大及多灶性心肌坏死和纤维化。它经典地好发于低硒土壤地区的儿童和育龄期女性,若不治疗可致死。目前认为,coxsackievirus(柯萨奇病毒)是在硒耗竭宿主体内触发急性型的协同因素。大骨节病会破坏生长板和关节软骨,导致手指缩短、踝、膝、腕和肘关节变形,并造成永久性活动受限。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 早期克山病对补硒治疗反应良好,如果能在心肌发生重构之前发现,心力衰竭可以显著改善甚至逆转。一旦发展为伴有确立性纤维化的扩张型心肌病,心肌损伤就无法完全逆转,预后较差。大骨节病造成的软骨坏死及由此产生的关节畸形是永久性的。在中国流行地区预防性给予亚硒酸钠可预防新发病例,这是因果方向成立的最有力证据。
items.at_risk_zh: 居住在低硒土壤带的人群,主要是从中国东北到西南呈对角线分布的地带,以及西伯利亚部分地区。长期接受未额外添加硒的肠外营养者。重度吸收不良、短肠综合征和囊性纤维化患者。透析患者。对于在北美这样土壤硒含量高的地区进食混合膳食的人来说,饮食性硒缺乏并不是现实的担忧;仅两颗巴西坚果所含的硒量就已超过成人RDA。
items.prevalence_zh: 无确切数据,没有目前的全球数字。克山病曾在中国特定的低硒地区呈地方性流行,自20世纪70年代开始补充亚硒酸钠并改变食物供应结构以来,发病率已降至接近零。在美国,单靠膳食摄入的硒中位数已超过RDA,饮食性硒缺乏基本不存在。

items.function_short_zh: 数百种反应的辅因子;每一分子ATP都要与镁结合才能发挥作用。
items.function_full_zh: ATP在生物学上真正起作用的形式是Mg-ATP,因此镁是每一个激酶反应、每一种ATP酶以及DNA和RNA聚合酶所必需的参与者,总共涉及300多种酶。镁也是一种生理性的钙拮抗剂:静息状态下它会阻断NMDA受体通道,并减少血管平滑肌和心肌中的钙内流,这就是为什么镁缺乏会提高神经肌肉兴奋性并增加心律失常风险。甲状旁腺激素的分泌以及靶器官对它的反应也都需要镁,因此镁缺乏会导致低钙血症,而这种低钙血症在镁被补足之前无法纠正。人体内约60%的镁储存在骨骼中,其余大部分位于细胞内,血清中仅占约1%。因此血清镁并不能很好地反映体内总镁状态,即使一个人真正处于镁缺乏状态,血清镁也可能正常。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 症状性低镁血症(ICD-10编码E83.4)。这种缺乏没有专有病名;其重度表现为低镁血症性手足搐搦,伴顽固性低钙血症和低钾血症。遗传性肾性镁消耗(Gitelman综合征、伴高钙尿症的家族性低镁血症)属于遗传性肾小管疾病,而非饮食缺乏所致。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 通常完全没有症状。摄入不足表现为摄入量低于估计平均需要量,而血清镁仍然正常,因为肾脏会积极地保留镁。人们最先察觉到的是肌肉痉挛、眼睑或手部震颤,以及易怒或睡眠不佳,这些症状都是非特异性的。实际上,血清镁偏低最常是在因不明原因低钾血症或低钙血症而进行的代谢检查中偶然发现的。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 手足搐搦伴Chvostek征和Trousseau征阳性、感觉异常、癫痫发作,以及包括心房颤动和torsades de pointes(尖端扭转型室速)在内的心律失常。伴随的低钾血症和低钙血症在镁本身被补足之前难以纠正,这是临床上重要的教学要点。重度病例几乎总是由药物、消化道或肾脏丢失所致,而非单纯饮食因素。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 补镁可以纠正神经肌肉和心脏方面的表现,并使相关的钾、钙异常随之恢复,只要根本病因得到处理,就不会留下残余缺陷。唯一需要注意的是时机问题,而非不可逆性:血清镁会先于体内总储量恢复正常,骨骼和细胞内的镁库需要数天到数周才能补足,过早停止补充会让缺乏再次出现。
items.at_risk_zh: 长期饮酒是主要病因之一。慢性腹泻、吸收不良、短肠综合征以及减重手术后。长期使用质子泵抑制剂,可导致严重低镁血症。袢利尿剂和噻嗪类利尿剂、顺铂、两性霉素以及钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂。血糖控制不佳伴渗透性利尿的糖尿病。再喂养综合征。对于肾脏和肠道功能均正常的人来说,单靠饮食很少会导致症状性镁缺乏。
items.prevalence_zh: 各年龄段美国人中,约48%从食物和饮料中摄入的镁低于其估计平均需要量(NHANES 2013-2016)。具有临床意义的低镁血症远比这一数字所暗示的少见:一般人群中约为2.5%至15%,住院患者中升至约10%至20%,重症监护患者中更高。这两个数字之间的差距,正是低摄入量常被夸大为普遍性缺乏的原因。

items.supplement: Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet
items.function_short_zh: 构建骨矿物质,并传递肌肉收缩、神经冲动和凝血所需的信号。
items.function_full_zh: 人体内约99%的钙以hydroxyapatite(羟磷灰石)晶体形式存在于骨骼和牙齿中,起结构支撑作用。其余约1%是细胞通用的第二信使:触发肌肉的兴奋收缩偶联、突触处神经递质的释放,以及凝血级联反应中的若干步骤。血清游离钙由甲状旁腺激素、calcitriol(骨化三醇)和骨吸收共同维持在一个非常狭窄的范围内,因此饮食摄入不足并不会降低血钙,而是由骨骼买单来补偿。这种调节机制正是本条目的关键所在。分级吸收率会随摄入量升高而下降,因此对已经通过食物满足需求量的人来说,额外补充的钙对骨矿物质的贡献很小,多余部分大多被排出体外。补充剂相较于食物真正增加的是一次性摄入的大剂量吸收负荷,这正是便秘、Women's Health Initiative研究(妇女健康倡议研究)中观察到的肾结石风险升高,以及尚有争议的心血管信号的背景所在。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 儿童缺钙性佝偻病和成人骨软化症,伴营养性继发性甲状旁腺功能亢进。这是真正摄入不足所导致的疾病,与饮食本已充足的人是否额外补钙无关。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 没有任何自觉症状。生化指标上,甲状旁腺激素升高而血清钙保持正常,尿钙下降,骨转换标志物升高。骨骼正在被悄悄消耗,这也是为什么早期阶段总是只在因其他原因进行检查时才被偶然发现。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 儿童表现为佝偻病,包括腿部弯曲、腕部和肋软骨连接处增宽、骨痛和生长迟缓。成人表现为骨软化症,包括弥漫性骨痛、近端肌无力和假性骨折,数十年后骨量丢失加速,脆性骨折风险增加。伴手足搐搦和感觉异常的症状性低钙血症,通常源于甲状旁腺或维生素D功能障碍,而不是单纯饮食摄入不足,因为骨骼对摄入量的缓冲作用非常有效。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 佝偻病和骨软化症在补钙(如果同时缺乏维生素D,也一并补充)后可以痊愈,骨矿物质密度大部分能够恢复。但有两点无法完全恢复:生长期儿童已经形成的骨骼畸形及因此损失的身高,以及青春期未能积累到的骨峰值量,后者决定了一生的骨量基线,日后补充也无法弥补。
items.at_risk_zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲和南亚部分地区,饮食低钙、高植酸的儿童,已有记录显示其膳食摄入量约为每日200毫克。不吃乳制品也没有强化替代品的成人。吸收不良、胃切除术后状态、长期使用皮质类固醇,以及未经治疗的乳糜泻患者。本条目所描述的人群,即饮食本已满足需求量的人,按定义就不属于风险人群,这正是本条目要强调的重点。
items.prevalence_zh: 针对钙特异性缺乏,无确切的全球数据,因为在调查数据中很难将其与维生素D缺乏区分开来。但在地区层面已有充分记录:患营养性佝偻病的尼日利亚儿童,膳食钙摄入量中位数约为每日203毫克(对照组为196毫克,P=0.64),而按年龄不同,需要量大约为每日700至1300毫克;在治疗中,单独补钙的效果优于单独补充维生素D。

items.function_short_zh: 不是营养素。口腔和肠道细菌将其转化为一氧化氮,从而使血管扩张。
items.function_full_zh: 来自甜菜根和绿叶蔬菜的无机硝酸盐在小肠近端被吸收,循环池中约四分之一会被唾液腺主动浓缩。舌根部的共生细菌将其还原为亚硝酸盐,吞咽下的亚硝酸盐随后在酸性胃环境及缺氧组织中,经脱氧血红蛋白、脱氧肌红蛋白、xanthine oxidoreductase(黄嘌呤氧化还原酶)等金属蛋白进一步还原为一氧化氮。这条肠道唾液循环途径是一条补充性供应线路,与人体自身由nitric oxide synthase(一氧化氮合酶,NOS)以L-精氨酸合成一氧化氮的主要且始终可用的途径并行运作。正是这一区别使硝酸盐成为一种可利用的底物,而非必需营养素:即使饮食中不含硝酸盐,NOS来源的一氧化氮合成也照常进行。已测得的效应属于药理性且具有剂量依赖性:血管扩张并伴血压小幅下降,以及亚极量运动时耗氧量降低。抗菌漱口水会通过杀灭还原硝酸盐的口腔菌群而完全消除这一效应,这最清楚地表明其机制是微生物性的,而非营养性的。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。没有人会缺乏膳食硝酸盐,因为人体对它没有需求,并能独立合成一氧化氮。不吃甜菜根也不吃绿叶蔬菜的人,血浆亚硝酸盐水平较低,会错失血压下降和运动经济性提升的效应,但这属于错过了一种药理性益处,而不是一种缺乏状态。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用。膳食硝酸盐不是必需营养素,也不存在缺乏状态,因此不存在患病率数据,也不应引用任何数字。若要说明效应大小而非缺乏程度,汇总试验数据显示收缩压平均下降约3至5 mmHg,在高血压参与者中降幅最大。

items: ALA from flaxseed, chia or walnut oil
Wheat bran and insoluble fibre supplements for IBS

items.function_short: Long-chain fats built into brain, retina and heart cell membranes; they also help resolve inflammation.
items.function_full: EPA (20:5n-3) and DHA (22:6n-3) are the long-chain products of omega-3 metabolism. DHA is the dominant structural fatty acid of retinal photoreceptor outer segments and neuronal synaptic membranes, where it sets membrane fluidity and supports the function of embedded proteins such as rhodopsin. EPA is the substrate for series-3 prostaglandins and series-5 leukotrienes, and both are precursors of the resolvins and protectins that actively terminate inflammation. Because the body can make them from alpha-linolenic acid, they are classed as conditionally essential rather than strictly essential; the conversion is inefficient enough that tissue levels track intake of preformed EPA and DHA closely.
items.deficiency_name: NONE. No named clinical deficiency disease exists for EPA and DHA specifically, because they can be synthesised from ALA.
items.deficiency_early: Nothing a person would notice. The first measurable change is biochemical: a falling omega-3 index, meaning EPA plus DHA as a percentage of red cell fatty acids. Values at or below about 4% define the low band and 8% or above was the proposed target (Harris and von Schacky, PMID 15208005). Symptoms sometimes attributed to low omega-3 status, such as dry skin or low mood, are non-specific and have not been shown to track the index.
items.deficiency_severe: There is no severe clinical syndrome attributable to low EPA and DHA alone in an adult who is otherwise fed. Frank neurological deficiency signs belong to total omega-3 deprivation, which is an ALA problem (see that entry). The clearest documented consequence of low long-chain omega-3 supply is developmental: preterm infants cut off from third-trimester placental DHA transfer accrete far less retinal and brain DHA, with fetal accretion roughly doubling in the last five weeks of gestation.
items.reversibility_note: In adults repletion is complete. Red cell EPA and DHA rise over roughly three to four months, approximately the erythrocyte lifespan, and normalise fully with sustained intake. The partial designation covers the perinatal window only: in rhesus monkeys deprived of n-3 before birth, brain phospholipids had normalised by three years but retinal DHA reached only 84% of controls, although visual acuity thresholds were normal.
items.at_risk: People who eat no oily fish and take no supplement. Vegans and vegetarians, who have no direct dietary source of preformed EPA or DHA. Preterm infants. Carriers of FADS1/FADS2 minor alleles, who have lower desaturase activity and convert ALA less efficiently.
items.prevalence: Not a disease rate. As a status distribution, omega-3 index values at or below 4% are typical across North America, Central and South America, Europe, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Africa, while levels above 8% occur mainly around the Sea of Japan, in Scandinavia and in some indigenous coastal populations, based on 298 studies (Stark et al., PMID 27216485).
items.source: PMID 15208005 (Harris WS, von Schacky C. Prev Med. 2004); PMID 27216485 (Stark KD et al. Prog Lipid Res. 2016)

items.supplement: ALA from flaxseed, chia or walnut oil
items.function_short: The one omega-3 fat the body cannot make; the raw material for EPA and DHA.
items.function_full: Alpha-linolenic acid (18:3n-3) is a genuine essential nutrient. Humans lack the desaturase that places a double bond at the n-3 position of a fatty acid, so every omega-3 molecule in the body traces back to dietary ALA or to preformed EPA and DHA. ALA is incorporated into membrane phospholipids, is a substantial oxidative fuel (a large share of an ingested dose is simply burned), and is the substrate for the elongation and desaturation pathway producing EPA, DPA and DHA. Stable-isotope tracer work puts net conversion to EPA at about 8% in young men and 21% in young women, with DHA formation around 9% in women and undetectable in men (PMID 12323085, PMID 12323090). The US Adequate Intake is 1.6 g/day for men and 1.1 g/day for women.
items.deficiency_name: Alpha-linolenic acid deficiency, the n-3 form of essential fatty acid deficiency (EFAD). It is a recognised clinical entity but carries no eponym comparable to scurvy or rickets.
items.deficiency_early: Biochemically, a rising ratio of n-6 to n-3 fatty acids in plasma and red cell phospholipids with falling 22:6n-3, detectable before any symptom. Clinically, the first reported signs in humans were sensory: intermittent numbness and paraesthesia in the limbs, and blurring of vision.
items.deficiency_severe: In the index case, a six-year-old girl maintained on parenteral nutrition rich in linoleate but nearly devoid of linolenate developed, after five months, episodes of numbness, paraesthesia, leg pain, weakness, inability to walk and blurred vision (Holman et al., PMID 6801965). Patients on long-term gastric-tube feeding with n-3-poor formulas developed scaly dermatitis and a haemorrhagic folliculitis (Bjerve et al.). Deficiency of this severity effectively arises only when the entire fat supply is medically controlled.
items.reversibility_note: In every documented human case, neurological symptoms disappeared and skin lesions resolved once an n-3-containing lipid source was substituted, with plasma fatty acid profiles normalising alongside. No residual deficit was reported. The honest caveat is that all reported cases were identified within months; the consequences of much longer deprivation in humans are unknown.
items.at_risk: Patients on long-term parenteral nutrition or tube feeding with lipid sources low in n-3, historically safflower-based emulsions. Essentially nobody eating ordinary food, since ALA is widespread in vegetable oils, nuts, seeds and green leaves. Extremely low-fat diets sustained for years are a theoretical risk with no case series behind it.
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED. Clinical ALA deficiency exists only in case reports and small series of parenteral and tube-fed patients. No population prevalence figure exists because the condition does not occur in free-living people eating normal diets.
items.source: PMID 6801965 (Holman RT, Johnson SB, Hatch TF. Am J Clin Nutr. 1982;35:617-23); PMID 12323085 and PMID 12323090 (Burdge GC et al. Br J Nutr. 2002); Institute of Medicine DRI for Macronutrients 2005, doi:10.17226/10490

items.function_short: Oil from marine microalgae that supplies ready-made DHA, and in some products EPA, without fish.
items.function_full: Algal oil is extracted from cultured heterotrophic microalgae, chiefly Schizochytrium species and Crypthecodinium cohnii. These are the organisms at the base of the marine food chain that actually synthesise DHA; fish accumulate it by eating them. Crypthecodinium products supply DHA only, while Schizochytrium products supply DHA plus a smaller amount of EPA. Physiologically the oil does nothing that DHA and EPA do not do, so the mechanism sits in the Omega-3 (EPA and DHA) entry. Controlled feeding work found algal-oil capsules and cooked salmon to be nutritionally equivalent sources of DHA in terms of plasma incorporation (PMID 18589030), which is why algal DHA has been the standard source in infant formula for decades.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. Algal oil is a manufactured delivery form, not a nutrient, and nobody becomes deficient in it. The status question that matters is DHA and EPA status, answered in the Omega-3 (EPA and DHA) entry.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE as a deficiency. As a practical supply point, algal oil is the only direct dietary source of preformed DHA for people who eat no fish, since ALA conversion yields little DHA in women and none detectable in men.
items.source: PMID 18589030 (Arterburn LM et al. J Am Diet Assoc. 2008;108:1204-9)

items.function_short: Oil from Antarctic krill delivering EPA and DHA largely bound to phospholipids, plus some astaxanthin.
items.function_full: Krill oil is extracted from Euphausia superba. Its distinguishing feature is chemical form: a large share of the EPA and DHA is esterified to phospholipid, mainly phosphatidylcholine, with some present as free fatty acid, whereas fish oil carries them as triglycerides or ethyl esters. This alters absorption kinetics. It also contains small amounts of astaxanthin, a carotenoid acting as an antioxidant within the oil. EPA plus DHA content per capsule is typically lower than in fish oil, so dose comparisons need to be made per milligram of omega-3. Acute crossover studies find equal or modestly higher plasma phospholipid incorporation from krill per unit EPA plus DHA (PMID 21854650), but a reanalysis of these studies concluded the acute differences have not translated reliably into different long-term omega-3 status (PMID 25156381).
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. Krill oil is a manufactured product category, not an essential nutrient, and no deficiency state exists for it. The relevant physiology is EPA and DHA status, covered in the Omega-3 (EPA and DHA) entry.
items.source: PMID 21854650 (Schuchardt JP et al. Lipids Health Dis. 2011); PMID 25156381 (Salem N Jr, Kuratko CN. Lipids Health Dis. 2014)

items.function_short: Concentrated food protein supplying the amino acids used to build and repair muscle and every tissue.
items.function_full: Protein powder is isolated food protein (whey, casein, soy, pea, rice, egg) dried and concentrated. It has no function of its own; the function is that of dietary protein, which supplies the nine indispensable amino acids plus nitrogen for synthesis of muscle, enzymes, albumin, immunoglobulins, haemoglobin, hormones and connective tissue. An adult turns over roughly 250 to 300 g of body protein daily, most of it recycled, with dietary intake covering obligatory oxidative losses. The US RDA is 0.8 g/kg/day. The PROT-AGE group recommends 1.0 to 1.2 g/kg/day for healthy older adults and 1.2 to 1.5 g/kg/day in acute or chronic illness, because the muscle protein synthetic response to a given protein dose is blunted with age (PMID 23867520).
items.deficiency_name: Kwashiorkor and marasmus, the two poles of severe acute malnutrition, with marasmic kwashiorkor in between. Protein-energy malnutrition is the umbrella term. Sarcopenia is the chronic age-related deficit state.
items.deficiency_early: Unintentional weight loss, falling mid-upper arm circumference, loss of subcutaneous fat and muscle bulk, thinning brittle hair, delayed wound healing and more frequent infections. Serum albumin falls late and is heavily confounded by inflammation, so it is a poor early marker. In older adults, declining grip strength and slower gait speed usually appear before visible muscle loss.
items.deficiency_severe: Marasmus is severe wasting: weight-for-height far below normal, visible loss of muscle and fat, an aged appearance in a young child. Kwashiorkor adds pitting oedema, an enlarged fatty liver, flaky-paint skin desquamation and hair depigmentation. Both carry high case fatality from hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, electrolyte disturbance and overwhelming infection; without structured refeeding the endpoint is death. In older adults, untreated sarcopenia ends in falls, fracture, loss of independence and raised mortality.
items.reversibility_note: Acute wasting reverses with careful staged refeeding, and weight-for-height recovers. What does not fully recover is linear growth and neurocognitive development when the episode falls within the first 1000 days: stunting established before age two is largely permanent, and the associated cognitive deficits persist into adulthood. Sarcopenia is partly reversible, since resistance training with adequate protein rebuilds strength and some mass, but muscle lost over decades is not fully regained.
items.at_risk: Children in food-insecure settings, especially around weaning and following infection. Hospitalised, post-surgical and critically ill patients. Older adults with poor appetite, dental problems, dysphagia or social isolation. People with malabsorption, cirrhosis, or cachexia from cancer, advanced kidney or heart failure. Anorexia nervosa. Healthy adults in wealthy countries eating adequate calories almost never fall short of protein.
items.prevalence: In 2024, 42.8 million children under five were wasted (6.6%) and 12.2 million severely wasted (1.9%); 150.2 million were stunted (UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Joint Malnutrition Estimates, 2025 edition). Sarcopenia prevalence in older adults ranges roughly 10% to 27% depending on diagnostic criteria, with the lower end corresponding to EWGSOP2.
items.source: UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Joint Child Malnutrition Estimates 2025 (https://data.unicef.org/resources/jme/); PMID 23867520 (Bauer J et al. PROT-AGE. J Am Med Dir Assoc. 2013;14:542-59); doi:10.1007/s40520-021-01951-7 (sarcopenia prevalence under EWGSOP1 and EWGSOP2, Aging Clin Exp Res. 2021)

items.function_short: An amino acid the body makes itself; a preferred fuel for gut lining and immune cells.
items.function_full: Glutamine is the most abundant free amino acid in plasma and skeletal muscle. Muscle synthesises and exports it continuously via glutamine synthetase, so supply is normally set by endogenous production rather than by diet. Enterocytes and rapidly dividing immune cells use it as a preferred respiratory fuel and as the nitrogen donor for purine, pyrimidine and glutathione synthesis, which is the biochemistry behind the gut-repair claim. It is classed as non-essential in health and conditionally essential in severe catabolic states, where muscle export cannot keep pace with consumption. Human trials of oral glutamine for intestinal permeability, IBS and inflammatory bowel disease have been small and inconsistent, and the strongest evidence is in specific clinical contexts rather than in healthy people.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no dietary requirement for glutamine and therefore no dietary deficiency to detect. Low plasma glutamine arises as a consequence of critical illness, major trauma or burns, not of what someone eats.
items.deficiency_severe: NOT APPLICABLE. Plasma glutamine below roughly 420 micromol/L in ICU patients is associated with higher mortality, but it marks the severity of catabolism rather than a nutrient shortfall. Treating it as a deficiency to correct proved harmful: in the REDOXS trial of 1223 ventilated ICU patients with multi-organ failure, high-dose glutamine increased in-hospital and six-month mortality (PMID 23594003).
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. Nobody becomes glutamine-deficient from diet. Low plasma concentrations occur in sepsis, major burns, major trauma and prolonged critical illness, and reflect the underlying illness.
items.source: PMID 23594003 (Heyland D et al. N Engl J Med. 2013;368:1489-97)

items.function_short: Hydrolysed animal collagen eaten as protein; the body builds its own collagen from ordinary amino acids.
items.function_full: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the body, roughly a third of total body protein, forming the tensile framework of skin, tendon, ligament, bone matrix, cartilage and vessel wall. The body synthesises it from ordinary amino acids as a repeating Gly-X-Y sequence rich in proline; the post-translational hydroxylation that stabilises the triple helix is carried out by prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases, which require vitamin C, iron and 2-oxoglutarate. Ingested collagen is digested like any other protein, though some di- and tripeptides such as prolyl-hydroxyproline do reach the bloodstream intact, which is the proposed mechanism for any effect beyond amino acid supply. As a protein source collagen is nutritionally incomplete: it contains no tryptophan and is low in several other indispensable amino acids.
items.deficiency_name: NONE. Scurvy is sometimes described loosely as a collagen deficiency, which is a misreading: it is vitamin C deficiency, and the defective collagen is downstream of the missing enzyme cofactor.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. Collagen is not a dietary requirement and there is no dietary collagen deficiency. Real failures of collagen come from vitamin C deficiency (scurvy), from inherited defects in collagen genes (osteogenesis imperfecta, the Ehlers-Danlos syndromes), or from overall protein-energy malnutrition. None of these is corrected by eating collagen.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. One theoretical argument deserves mention without overstatement: a stoichiometric analysis calculated that endogenous glycine synthesis plus typical dietary glycine falls roughly 10 g/day short of the amount required for maximal collagen turnover in a 70 kg adult (PMID 20093739). This remains a calculation. No glycine or collagen deficiency state has been demonstrated clinically.
items.source: PMID 20093739 (Melendez-Hevia E et al. J Biosci. 2009;34:853-72); NCBI Bookshelf NBK507709 (Biochemistry, Collagen Synthesis, StatPearls)

items.function_short: A gel-forming fibre that holds water in stool, making it softer, bulkier and easier to pass.
items.function_full: Psyllium is the milled seed husk of Plantago ovata, largely a highly branched arabinoxylan that is gel-forming and, unusually among viscous fibres, poorly fermented by colonic bacteria. Because it survives intact to the rectum it retains its water there, producing bulky soft stool with far less gas than fermentable fibres. It normalises stool form in both directions, softening hard stool and firming loose stool. The same gel raises the viscosity of small intestinal contents, which slows glucose absorption and traps bile acids; the resulting loss of bile acids drives hepatic synthesis from cholesterol and lowers LDL. In IBS it is the fibre with actual trial support: ispaghula gave a relative risk of IBS not improving of 0.83 (95% CI 0.73 to 0.94), number needed to treat 7 (95% CI 4 to 25), and is the fibre recommended by the ACG guideline (PMID 33315591).
items.deficiency_early: There is no psyllium deficiency; psyllium is one way to correct a shortfall in total dietary fibre. Low fibre intake shows up first as harder and less frequent stools, straining, longer whole-gut transit time and reduced stool weight.
items.deficiency_severe: No deficiency disease follows from low fibre intake. What the evidence supports is a graded association: pooling 185 prospective studies and 58 trials, the highest fibre intake groups had 15% to 30% lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality than the lowest, with lower incidence of coronary heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer. Benefit accrued across 25 to 29 g/day with more above 30 g/day (Reynolds et al., PMID 30638909). Untreated chronic constipation can itself progress to faecal impaction and, rarely, stercoral ulceration or perforation.
items.reversibility_note: Stool form, frequency, transit time and the LDL and post-prandial glucose effects all correct within days to a few weeks of adequate intake, and revert when intake stops. The mortality and cancer associations relate to long-term dietary pattern rather than to short-term supplementation, and no trial has shown a fibre supplement reverses established colorectal neoplasia.
items.at_risk: For low total fibre intake: most people eating a Western diet, particularly those eating mainly refined grains with few vegetables, pulses or fruit, and anyone on a prolonged low-residue or restrictive diet. Mean US adult intake is about 16 g/day against an Adequate Intake of 25 g/day for younger women and 38 g/day for younger men.
items.prevalence: Roughly 5% of the US population meets the fibre Adequate Intake, and 7.4% of US adults meet 14 g per 1000 kcal, on NHANES data; mean intake is about 16 g/day. No figure exists for psyllium specifically because it is a supplement rather than a nutrient.
items.source: PMID 30638909 (Reynolds A et al. Lancet. 2019;393:434-45); PMID 33315591 (Lacy BE et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Management of IBS. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:17-44); NHANES fiber intake data brief, NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559

items.function_short: Fibres your gut bacteria feed on, boosting bifidobacteria and producing short-chain fatty acids in the colon.
items.function_full: Inulin and fructo-oligosaccharides are fructose polymers from chicory root, Jerusalem artichoke, onion, garlic and wheat, differing mainly in chain length: FOS has a degree of polymerisation below about 9, inulin extends to 60. GOS are galactose oligomers produced enzymatically from lactose and are structural analogues of human milk oligosaccharides. All three resist human digestive enzymes, reach the colon intact and are selectively fermented, reproducibly raising Bifidobacterium abundance, which is the basis of the ISAPP definition of a prebiotic as a substrate selectively used by host microorganisms to confer a health benefit (PMID 28611480). Fermentation yields acetate, propionate and butyrate; butyrate is the primary respiratory fuel of the colonocyte, and the short-chain fatty acid pool lowers luminal pH and supports barrier function. That same fermentability produces the gas and bloating these compounds are known for, and is why they are classed as high-FODMAP.
items.deficiency_early: No prebiotic-specific deficiency exists. Low intake of fermentable substrate lowers colonic short-chain fatty acid production, particularly butyrate, and reduces Bifidobacterium abundance. Both are measurable in stool and neither produces a symptom a person would notice.
items.deficiency_severe: There is no severe deficiency syndrome in humans. The strongest mechanistic finding comes from mice: under chronic or intermittent fibre deprivation the microbiota switches to degrading host-secreted mucus glycoproteins, thinning the colonic mucus barrier and increasing susceptibility to an enteric pathogen (Desai et al., PMID 27863247). This has not been shown to produce disease in people, and the human outcomes attributed to low fibre intake are best assessed at the level of total fibre rather than prebiotics specifically.
items.reversibility_note: Bifidobacterium abundance and short-chain fatty acid output respond within days to about a week of intake and return toward baseline over a similar period after stopping. The effect is intake-dependent throughout, and no durable change in microbiota composition persists once supplementation ends.
items.at_risk: Anyone eating little onion, garlic, leek, chicory, wheat, banana or legume. People following a low-FODMAP diet for IBS restrict precisely these substrates and show measurable falls in Bifidobacterium, which is why the restriction phase is intended to be time-limited and followed by structured reintroduction. Infants on formulas without added GOS or FOS receive none.
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED. No requirement has been set for prebiotics, so no adequacy figure exists. Habitual inulin-type fructan intake in Europe and the US is estimated at roughly 1 to 10 g/day.
items.source: PMID 28611480 (Gibson GR et al. ISAPP consensus statement on prebiotics. Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2017;14:491-502); PMID 27863247 (Desai MS et al. Cell. 2016;167:1339-53)

items.supplement: Wheat bran and insoluble fibre supplements for IBS
items.function_short: Coarse insoluble fibre that adds stool bulk mechanically; in IBS it often makes symptoms worse.
items.function_full: Wheat bran is the outer layer of the wheat kernel, composed mainly of insoluble arabinoxylan, cellulose and lignin. It acts through particle bulk and mechanical stimulation of the mucosa rather than by forming a gel: coarse particles increase stool mass and provoke secretion and peristalsis, whereas finely ground bran loses this effect and can slow transit. It holds far less water than psyllium and is partly fermented, generating gas. In IBS these properties work against the patient, since mechanical stimulation acts on a hypersensitive gut and bran also carries fructans, making it high-FODMAP. Meta-analysis found no significant benefit of bran for global IBS symptoms (relative risk of not improving 0.90, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.03), in contrast to ispaghula (NNT 7), and the ACG guideline recommends soluble fibre for IBS (PMID 33315591).
items.deficiency_early: There is no wheat bran deficiency. The functional label applies to total dietary fibre, where low intake produces harder and less frequent stools, straining, reduced stool weight and slower whole-gut transit. Withdrawing bran from someone for whom it was the only fibre source reproduces these effects.
items.deficiency_severe: Nothing severe follows from not taking a bran supplement. The general low-fibre associations apply: 15% to 30% lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in the highest versus lowest total fibre intake groups, with lower coronary heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer incidence (PMID 30638909). In IBS specifically the more common clinical problem runs the other way. Among 100 consecutive IBS referrals who had tried bran, 55% reported it made them worse and only 10% found it helpful, with bowel disturbance, distension and pain all exacerbated (Francis and Whorwell, PMID 7912305).
items.reversibility_note: Stool bulk, frequency and transit time respond within days of changing insoluble fibre intake and revert on withdrawal. Bran-induced symptom flares in IBS settle once bran is stopped, and no lasting mucosal or functional damage has been described.
items.at_risk: For low total fibre intake: people eating predominantly refined grains with few plant foods, with mean US adult intake around 16 g/day against an Adequate Intake of 25 to 38 g/day. For harm rather than shortfall: people with IBS, who are the population most likely to be given bran and most likely to be worsened by it.
items.prevalence: About 5% of the US population meets the fibre Adequate Intake, mean intake around 16 g/day (NHANES). For bran intolerance in IBS, 55% of 100 consecutive IBS referrals reported symptom worsening on bran (PMID 7912305).
items.source: PMID 7912305 (Francis CY, Whorwell PJ. Lancet. 1994;344:39-40); PMID 30638909 (Reynolds A et al. Lancet. 2019;393:434-45); PMID 33315591 (Lacy BE et al. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:17-44)

errors.correction: The cited paper does not contain a 10-27% range and does not put EWGSOP2 at the lower end of one. Fernandes LV et al. (Aging Clin Exp Res. 2022;34:505-514, doi:10.1007/s40520-021-01951-7, online 2021, so the year given is also off) reports overall prevalence of 17.7% by EWGSOP1 and 11% by EWGSOP2, with study-level ranges of 6.2-35.3% (EWGSOP1) and 3.2-26.3% (EWGSOP2). The EWGSOP2 range starts at 3.2%, well below 10%, so 'lower end corresponding to EWGSOP2' is not supportable from this source. The 10-27% figure the entry is actually reproducing comes from a different paper, Petermann-Rocha F et al., Global prevalence of sarcopenia and severe sarcopenia, J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle. 2022;13:86-99. Either cite Petermann-Rocha for 10-27%, or restate as '17.7% under EWGSOP1 and 11% under EWGSOP2' and keep the current citation.
errors.source: Fernandes LV et al., Aging Clin Exp Res. 2022;34:505-514 (doi:10.1007/s40520-021-01951-7), abstract retrieved via publisher listing; Petermann-Rocha F et al., J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle. 2022;13:86-99

errors.correction: Naming kwashiorkor as a deficiency state of dietary protein reproduces an aetiology the field abandoned. Waterlow and Payne's reanalysis, and subsequent work, found that children with kwashiorkor often have protein intakes comparable to marasmic children, that some affected children are still breastfed, and that high-protein repletion does not preferentially resolve it; the current view is that kwashiorkor is a multifactorial complication of severe malnutrition involving infection, oxidative stress and other factors that remain unexplained. Marasmus, wasting and protein-energy malnutrition are defensible as the protein deficiency state; kwashiorkor should be described as a form of severe acute malnutrition of uncertain aetiology, not as what happens when you eat too little protein.
errors.source: Waterlow JC and Payne PR, the protein gap reappraisal; StatPearls Kwashiorkor (NBK507876); The Conversation summary of the protein-gap error, all consistent that kwashiorkor is not attributable to relative protein deficiency

errors.correction: Listing sarcopenia as 'the chronic age-related deficit state' for protein presents a multifactorial geriatric syndrome as a nutrient deficiency. EWGSOP2 defines sarcopenia as a muscle disease driven by ageing, inactivity, inflammation, anabolic resistance and comorbidity; low protein intake is one modifiable risk factor among several, and sarcopenia occurs in older adults meeting the RDA. Reword to 'low protein intake is one contributor to sarcopenia' rather than naming sarcopenia as the deficiency state. The PROT-AGE citation and its 1.0-1.2 and 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day figures are correct and can stay.
errors.source: PMID 23867520 (Bauer J et al., PROT-AGE, J Am Med Dir Assoc. 2013;14:542-59), which frames higher protein as one component of sarcopenia prevention alongside exercise; EWGSOP2 operational definition

errors.correction: The note reports the two findings from the rhesus study that look reassuring and omits the one that does not. Anderson GJ, Neuringer M, Lin DS, Connor WE (Pediatr Res. 2005;58:865-72) found retinal DHA incomplete at 84% of controls and brain phospholipids normal at 3 years, and behavioural visual acuity thresholds normal at 4, 8 and 12 weeks, all as stated. But the same animals also showed persistently lower cone and rod ERG a-wave amplitudes, which is why the paper answers its own title question in the negative. Add the ERG finding: the residual after prenatal deprivation is functional as well as biochemical. The PARTIAL rating itself is correct and should stand.
errors.source: Anderson GJ et al., Can prenatal n-3 fatty acid deficiency be completely reversed after birth? Pediatr Res. 2005;58:865-72, doi:10.1203/01.pdr.0000182188.31596.5a

errors.correction: Both percentages are real but neither comes from the cited source. NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559 (FSRG Dietary Data Brief, WWEIA NHANES 2009-2010) supports the 16 g/day mean and nothing else; it explicitly does not report a percentage meeting the Adequate Intake. The 'roughly 5%' figure traces to Quagliani D and Felt-Gunderson P, Am J Lifestyle Med. 2017;11:80-85. The 7.4% figure traces to Miketinas DC et al., NHANES 2013-2018 usual fibre intake analysis. Cite those two directly. The same 5% and 16 g/day pairing is repeated in the Wheat bran entry's prevalence field with the same citation gap.
errors.source: NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559 (mean 16 g/day, no AI-attainment figure); Quagliani and Felt-Gunderson, Am J Lifestyle Med. 2017 (5%); Miketinas et al., NHANES 2013-2018 (7.4% meeting 14 g/1000 kcal)

errors.correction: 'Benefit accrued across 25 to 29 g/day with more above 30 g/day' states as established what Reynolds et al. offered as suggestive. The Lancet paper found the greatest risk reduction at intakes between 25 g and 29 g/day and said dose-response curves 'suggested that higher intakes of dietary fibre could confer even greater benefit'. Change to 'with dose-response curves suggesting, but not demonstrating, further benefit above 30 g/day'. Everything else in this field checks out: 185 prospective studies and 58 trials, and the 15-30% reduction across all-cause and cardiovascular mortality and CHD, stroke, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer incidence.
errors.source: PMID 30638909 (Reynolds A et al., Lancet. 2019;393:434-45)

errors.correction: The 420 micromol/L threshold is correct but uncited. The entry's only source is PMID 23594003 (REDOXS), which does not report that cut-off. It comes from Oudemans-van Straaten HM et al., Plasma glutamine depletion and patient outcome in acute ICU admissions, Intensive Care Med. 2001;27:84-90, PMID 11280678, which compared patients above and below 0.420 mmol/L in 80 non-elective ICU admissions. Add that citation. The REDOXS description is accurate as written: 1223 ventilated patients with multi-organ failure, higher in-hospital and 6-month mortality on glutamine.
errors.source: PMID 11280678 (Oudemans-van Straaten HM et al., Intensive Care Med. 2001;27:84-90); PMID 23594003 (Heyland D et al., N Engl J Med. 2013;368:1489-97)

misclassified.why: The entry contradicts its own label three times: deficiency_name is NONE, deficiency_early opens with 'No prebiotic-specific deficiency exists', and prevalence states 'No requirement has been set for prebiotics, so no adequacy figure exists'. A substance with no established requirement, no human deficiency state, and whose only severe-consequence evidence is a mouse mucus-barrier experiment (PMID 27863247, which the entry itself flags as unshown in people) cannot carry a FUNCTIONAL classification. This is the clearest overreach of the three fibre entries. The measurable falls in Bifidobacterium and faecal butyrate are pharmacodynamic responses to an intake, not a deficiency state.

misclassified.supplement: Wheat bran and insoluble fibre supplements for IBS
misclassified.why: The entry states outright that 'There is no wheat bran deficiency' and that 'The functional label applies to total dietary fibre', which concedes the label belongs to a different entity. Bran is a food fraction sold as a supplement, not a nutrient, and this is the one item in the group whose own cited trial evidence points to net harm in the named population (PMID 7912305: 55% of 100 consecutive IBS referrals worsened, 10% helped; PMID 33315591: bran RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.79-1.03, no benefit). Classifying it FUNCTIONAL implies a shortfall worth correcting with the product, which inverts the evidence.

Weakest of the three calls, but still inconsistent with how this dataset handles delivery forms. Algal oil and krill oil were correctly given NA/NONE on the reasoning that they are manufactured supply routes for a nutrient covered elsewhere. Psyllium is the same case for dietary fibre: the entry says 'There is no psyllium deficiency; psyllium is one way to correct a shortfall in total dietary fibre', and deficiency_name is NONE. The functional shortfall is real but belongs to total dietary fibre, which has no entry in this group. Either add a dietary fibre entry to carry the FUNCTIONAL label, or set all three fibre products to NONE and point them at it. Do not leave a FUNCTIONAL state paired with a NONE deficiency name.

chk.coverage: CLEAN. All 10 assigned names present exactly once, no extras, no duplicates.
chk.net: Strong dataset by the standard of this exercise. No invented deficiencies: all 16 PMIDs resolve to exactly the papers cited, and the entries that could have fabricated a deficiency state did not. L-glutamine and collagen peptides are correctly NONE, and the collagen entry pre-empts the classic error by naming scurvy as vitamin C deficiency and osteogenesis imperfecta and Ehlers-Danlos as genetic collagen defects that eating collagen does not touch. Priority 3 is clean throughout: no dietary deficiency is confused with a genetic disorder anywhere in the group, and the FADS1/FADS2 mention in the omega-3 entry is correctly framed as a conversion modifier, not a disorder. Reversibility, the field a reader acts on, survives checking in every case. ALA FULL is right (Holman's 6-year-old on Liposyn I resolved after linolenate was restored; Bjerve's tube-fed patients' dermatitis cleared within days of ethyl linolenate, and the growth-retarded case caught up). Protein PARTIAL is right, and correctly locates the irreversible part in first-1000-days stunting and cognition rather than in acute wasting. Omega-3 PARTIAL is right, though its note quietly drops the persistent ERG deficit from the very study it cites. The verified quantitative claims are unusually accurate: Burdge 8%/21%/9%/undetectable, ispaghula RR 0.83 with NNT 7 (95% CI 4-25) and bran RR 0.90 (0.79-1.03) from the ACG guideline, Francis and Whorwell 55% worse and 10% better in 100 referrals, JME 2025 at 42.8 million wasted (6.6%), 12.2 million severely wasted (1.9%) and 150.2 million stunted, Reynolds 185 studies and 58 trials, Stark 298 studies, and even the awkward 'DHA accretion roughly doubles in the last five weeks' claim, which is real. Real problems, in order: the sarcopenia prevalence range is attributed to a paper that reports different numbers (17.7% and 11%, ranges 6.2-35.3% and 3.2-26.3%) and does not support 'lower end corresponding to EWGSOP2'; kwashiorkor and sarcopenia are both named as protein deficiency states when neither is attributable to protein intake; three fibre products carry a FUNCTIONAL classification alongside a NONE deficiency name, inconsistent with how algal oil and krill oil were handled; and three correct numbers (5%, 7.4%, 420 micromol/L) sit under citations that do not carry them. Fix the sarcopenia prevalence line and the kwashiorkor naming first; those are the two a reader could repeat and be wrong about.

items.function_short_zh: 长链脂肪酸,是大脑、视网膜和心脏细胞膜的构成成分,也参与炎症的消退。
items.function_full_zh: EPA(20:5n-3)和DHA(22:6n-3)是omega-3代谢的长链产物。DHA是视网膜感光细胞外节和神经元突触膜的主要结构脂肪酸,决定膜的流动性,并支持视紫红质等嵌膜蛋白的功能。EPA是3系前列腺素和5系白三烯的底物,二者还是消退素和保护素的前体,这些介质主动终止炎症反应。由于人体可以由α亚麻酸合成EPA和DHA,二者被归类为条件必需脂肪酸,区别于严格必需脂肪酸。但转化效率有限,组织中的水平仍紧密跟随现成EPA和DHA的直接摄入量。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 无。EPA和DHA并没有专属命名的临床缺乏病,因为它们可以由ALA合成。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 本人通常察觉不到任何变化。最早可测得的改变是生化指标:omega-3指数下降,即EPA加DHA占红细胞脂肪酸的百分比。数值处于约4%或以下界定为低水平,8%或以上则是提出的目标值(Harris and von Schacky, PMID 15208005)。有时被归因于omega-3水平偏低的症状,例如皮肤干燥或情绪低落,均为非特异性表现,并未被证实与该指数存在对应关系。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 对于饮食其他方面正常的成年人,单纯EPA和DHA偏低并不会导致严重的临床综合征。明显的神经系统缺乏体征属于omega-3整体缺乏的范畴,那是ALA的问题(见该词条)。长链omega-3供应不足最明确记录的后果与发育有关:早产儿因中断了妊娠晚期胎盘DHA的转运,视网膜和大脑中蓄积的DHA明显更少,胎儿DHA蓄积速度在妊娠最后五周大约会翻倍。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 成年人的补充是完全可逆的。红细胞EPA和DHA水平在大约三到四个月内回升,大致相当于红细胞的寿命,并在持续摄入下完全恢复正常。部分可逆的判定仅适用于围产期这一窗口:在出生前被剥夺n-3脂肪酸的恒河猴中,到三岁时脑磷脂已恢复正常,行为学测得的视敏度阈值也正常,但视网膜DHA仅达到对照组的84%,视锥和视杆细胞的ERG a波振幅仍持续偏低,说明产前剥夺留下的缺陷既是生化层面的,也是功能层面的。
items.at_risk_zh: 不吃富脂鱼类且不服用补充剂的人。纯素食者和素食者,他们没有直接摄入现成EPA或DHA的膳食来源。早产儿。携带FADS1/FADS2次要等位基因的人,其desaturase活性较低,将ALA转化为EPA和DHA的效率也更低。
items.prevalence_zh: 这不是疾病发生率。作为一种状态分布,omega-3指数处于4%或以下在北美、中南美洲、欧洲、中东、东南亚和非洲较为常见,而8%以上的水平主要见于日本海周边、斯堪的纳维亚地区以及部分沿海原住民人群,数据基于298项研究(Stark et al., PMID 27216485)。

items.supplement: ALA from flaxseed, chia or walnut oil
items.function_short_zh: 人体唯一无法自行合成的omega-3脂肪,是合成EPA和DHA的原料。
items.function_full_zh: α亚麻酸(18:3n-3)是真正意义上的必需营养素。人体缺乏能在脂肪酸n-3位引入双键的desaturase,因此体内每一个omega-3分子都可追溯到膳食中的ALA,或直接摄入的现成EPA和DHA。ALA被整合进膜磷脂,也是重要的氧化燃料(摄入剂量中有相当一部分直接被氧化供能),同时也是生成EPA、DPA和DHA的延长与去饱和通路的底物。稳定同位素示踪研究显示,年轻男性中ALA向EPA的净转化率约为8%,年轻女性约为21%,DHA的生成率在女性中约为9%,在男性中则检测不到(PMID 12323085, PMID 12323090)。美国的适宜摄入量男性为1.6 g/day,女性为1.1 g/day。
items.deficiency_name_zh: α亚麻酸缺乏症,即必需脂肪酸缺乏症(EFAD)的n-3型。这是一种公认的临床病症,但没有像坏血病或佝偻病那样的专有病名。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 生化层面表现为血浆和红细胞磷脂中n-6与n-3脂肪酸比值升高,同时22:6n-3下降,这种变化在出现任何症状之前就可检测到。临床层面,人体病例中最早报告的体征属于感觉异常:肢体间歇性麻木和感觉异常,以及视物模糊。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 在首例报告中,一名六岁女童接受富含亚油酸盐但几乎不含亚麻酸盐的肠外营养,五个月后出现发作性麻木、感觉异常、腿痛、乏力、无法行走和视物模糊(Holman et al., PMID 6801965)。长期使用贫n-3配方经胃管喂养的患者出现了鳞屑性皮炎和出血性毛囊炎(Bjerve et al.)。只有在全部脂肪供应完全由医疗手段控制的情况下,才会出现这种严重程度的缺乏。
